docs.title: SwgohComlink
docs.text:
This project provides:

  • SwgohComlink for synchronous network calls to a running swgoh-comlink service.
  • SwgohComlinkAsync for asynchronous (async/await) network calls to the same service.
  • Typed clients in swgoh_comlink.typed, which return msgspec.Struct models (Player, Guild, …) instead of dicts, with raw=True for the v2 dict on any call.
  • RetryPolicy for opt-in retries of rate refusals and HTTP 503, and pacing of calls (see Retries and Pacing).
  • StatCalc / StatCalcAsync for local stat and GP calculation for game units.
  • GameDataBuilder / GameDataBuilderAsync for building StatCalc game data dynamically from Comlink.
  • Helpers — utility functions, constants, localization parsing, and data structures for working with game data.
  • Exceptions — custom exception hierarchy (SwgohComlinkException, SwgohComlinkValueError, SwgohComlinkTypeError, and the SwgohComlinkHTTPError family for HTTP error statuses) for error handling.

Both SwgohComlink and SwgohComlinkAsync share the same constructor parameters and public methods. The async client uses await for all requests and should be used inside an async with context manager.

For runnable code samples covering common tasks, see the Examples page. Coming from v2? The default import still returns dicts; see Migrating from v2 to v3 for what changed and the v3 alpha install guide for how to install it.

Similarly, StatCalcAsync provides an async factory method for non-blocking game data initialization, while inheriting all calculation methods from StatCalc.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Synchronous:

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, StatCalc

comlink = SwgohComlink(url="http://localhost:3000")
calc = StatCalc()

Asynchronous:

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlinkAsync, StatCalcAsync

async with SwgohComlinkAsync(host="127.0.0.1", port=3000) as comlink:
    calc = await StatCalcAsync.create()
    player = await comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)

docs.title: Choosing a Stats Method
docs.text:
SwgohComlink.get_unit_stats() and StatCalc.calc_player_stats() are similar in outcome but different in execution model:

  • SwgohComlink.get_unit_stats() calls an external swgoh-stats service over HTTP (stats_url). This legacy method relies on the use of a separate StatCalc Docker container.
  • StatCalc.calc_player_stats() runs calculations locally in-process using Python game data. It does not require the separate StatCalc Docker container. This is the recommended method.

Use get_unit_stats() when you already operate against hosted comlink/stat services. Use StatCalc.calc_player_stats() when you want local/offline control and no dependency on a separate stats container.

Both methods can be used in parallel, allowing for validation of results while migrating from the legacy approach to the native Python approach.

docs.title: Quick start
docs.text:
import asyncio
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlinkAsync

async def main():
    async with SwgohComlinkAsync() as comlink:
        player = await comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)

asyncio.run(main())

docs.title: Advanced CLI example
docs.text:
The streaming_guild_roster_advanced.py script accepts command-line arguments:

# Fetch by ally code with verbose timing
python streaming_guild_roster_advanced.py 314927874 -v

# Fetch by guild ID with debug output and 5 retries
python streaming_guild_roster_advanced.py <guild_id> -d -r 5

# Specify a remote Comlink host
python streaming_guild_roster_advanced.py 314927874 --host 192.168.1.100 --port 3200

Note

Examples using asyncio.TaskGroup (streaming_guild_roster*.py) require Python 3.11+.

docs.title: SwgohComlink Logging
docs.text:
The swgoh_comlink package follows Python's recommended best practice for library logging: it attaches only a NullHandler to the root package logger and never configures handlers, formatters, or log levels on its own.

This means:

  • By default the library is silent — no log output unless your application configures logging.
  • You have full control over formatting, log levels, and destinations.
  • No duplicate handlers or forced formatting from the library.

All loggers in the package use the swgoh_comlink namespace (e.g. swgoh_comlink.helpers, swgoh_comlink.exceptions), so you can target them by name.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
The simplest way to see log output is with logging.basicConfig():

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink

comlink = SwgohComlink()
player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)

This sends all DEBUG-and-above messages from every logger (including swgoh_comlink) to the console.

docs.title: Custom Console Handler
docs.text:
To control only swgoh_comlink output without affecting other loggers:

import logging
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink

comlink_logger = logging.getLogger("swgoh_comlink")
comlink_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.setFormatter(logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s"))
comlink_logger.addHandler(handler)

comlink = SwgohComlink()

docs.title: Using the Package's Built-in Formatter
docs.text:
The package ships a LoggingFormatter class in swgoh_comlink.globals that you can use as an opt-in convenience:

import logging
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.globals import LoggingFormatter

comlink_logger = logging.getLogger("swgoh_comlink")
comlink_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

handler = logging.StreamHandler()
handler.setFormatter(LoggingFormatter())
comlink_logger.addHandler(handler)

comlink = SwgohComlink()

docs.title: Rotating File Handler
docs.text:
To capture logs to a rotating file:

import logging
from logging.handlers import RotatingFileHandler
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink

comlink_logger = logging.getLogger("swgoh_comlink")
comlink_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)

file_handler = RotatingFileHandler(
    filename="./comlink.log",
    encoding="utf-8",
    maxBytes=2_500_000,
    backupCount=5,
)
file_handler.setFormatter(
    logging.Formatter("%(asctime)s - %(name)s - %(levelname)s - %(message)s")
)
comlink_logger.addHandler(file_handler)

comlink = SwgohComlink()

docs.title: Migration Guide
docs.text: This guide covers the changes needed when upgrading from swgoh_comlink v1.x (the requests-based release) to the new version that introduces async support, StatCalc, and httpx.

docs.title: 1. Update dependencies
docs.text:
The HTTP library changed from requests to httpx.

# Remove the old dependency
pip uninstall requests

# Install the new version
pip install --upgrade swgoh_comlink

If your project pins dependencies, update your requirements.txt or pyproject.toml:

- requests>=2.32.4
+ httpx>=0.28

httpx is installed automatically as a dependency of swgoh_comlink, so in most cases you only need to upgrade the package itself.

docs.title: 2. Update exception handling
docs.text:
v1.x let requests.RequestException escape on network failures. The client now catches the transport errors raised by httpx (httpx.RequestError: connection refused, timeouts, DNS failures) and re-raises them as SwgohComlinkException, so code that caught the requests exception must catch SwgohComlinkException instead. Do not switch it to httpx.RequestError; that exception never reaches your code.

  from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
- import requests
+ from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import SwgohComlinkException

  comlink = SwgohComlink()
  try:
      player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
- except requests.RequestException as e:
+ except SwgohComlinkException as e:
      print(f"Network error: {e}")

To tell argument errors apart from service and network errors, catch the subclasses first:

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import (
    SwgohComlinkException,
    SwgohComlinkValueError,
    SwgohComlinkTypeError,
)

comlink = SwgohComlink()
try:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
except SwgohComlinkValueError as e:
    print(f"Invalid argument value: {e}")
except SwgohComlinkTypeError as e:
    print(f"Invalid argument type: {e}")
except SwgohComlinkException as e:
    print(f"Comlink error: {e}")

The exception hierarchy is:

  • SwgohComlinkException — base for all library errors
    • SwgohComlinkValueError (also inherits ValueError) — invalid argument values
    • SwgohComlinkTypeError (also inherits TypeError) — invalid argument types
    • SwgohComlinkHTTPError — comlink answered with an HTTP error status (v2.3+)
      • SwgohComlinkRateLimitError — HTTP 429 or the game's Rate exceeded!
      • SwgohComlinkUnavailableError — HTTP 503
      • SwgohComlinkClientError — any other 4xx

See Exceptions for details.

docs.title: 3. Update logging configuration
docs.text:
The get_logger() helper no longer accepts a log_level parameter and no longer attaches handlers or sets log levels automatically. The library now follows Python best practice by attaching only a NullHandler to the package root logger.

Before:

from swgoh_comlink.globals import get_logger

logger = get_logger(__name__, log_level="DEBUG")  # auto-configured handler + level

After:

import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.DEBUG)  # configure logging in your application

Or target only the swgoh_comlink namespace:

import logging

comlink_logger = logging.getLogger("swgoh_comlink")
comlink_logger.setLevel(logging.DEBUG)
comlink_logger.addHandler(logging.StreamHandler())

See Logging for more examples including the built-in LoggingFormatter and rotating file handlers.

docs.title: 4. Close the client when done
docs.text:
The new version uses persistent httpx connection pools for better performance. This means the client should be closed when you are finished with it.

Context manager (recommended):

with SwgohComlink() as comlink:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
# connections are closed automatically

Manual close:

comlink = SwgohComlink()
try:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
finally:
    comlink.close()

Existing code that does not call close() will still work — connections are cleaned up on garbage collection — but explicitly closing is preferred to avoid resource warnings.

docs.title: 5. Helpers module refactoring
docs.text: The monolithic helpers.py file has been refactored into a helpers/ subpackage. All existing import paths continue to work — a backward-compatible re-export shim ensures no breaking changes.

docs.title: What moved
docs.text: Before After (internal location) helpers.py (single file) helpers/ subpackage with focused modules Constants.STAT_ENUMS helpers/_stat_data.STAT_ENUMS (re-exported) Constants.STATS helpers/_stat_data.STATS (re-exported) StatCalc.STATS_NAME_MAP Now imports from helpers/_stat_data.STATS

docs.title: Constants.get() changes
docs.text:
Constants.get() still works for all legacy PascalCase names (e.g., "UnitDefinitions") as well as the new UPPER_SNAKE_CASE DataItems names (e.g., "UNITS"):

from swgoh_comlink.helpers import Constants

# All three forms still work:
Constants.get("UnitDefinitions")  # -> '137438953472' (legacy name)
Constants.get("UNITS")            # -> '137438953472' (DataItems name)
Constants.get("Segment1")         # -> '2097151' (class attribute)

Recommendation: Prefer using DataItems enum values directly for type safety, request only the collections you need, and combine members with | — see GameDataItems server alignment below:

from swgoh_comlink.helpers import DataItems

items = DataItems.SKILL | DataItems.EQUIPMENT
data = comlink.get_game_data(items=items)

docs.title: Migration checker CLI
docs.text:
A CLI tool is included to scan your codebase for patterns that may need updating:

# Scan a project directory
python -m swgoh_comlink.migrate /path/to/your/project

# Or use the console script
swgoh-migrate /path/to/your/project

# Filter by severity and exclude directories
swgoh-migrate . --severity=WARNING --exclude .venv dist

The tool reports deprecated imports, removed APIs, and suggests replacements.

docs.title: 6. Subclass and internal API changes
docs.text: These only matter if you subclass SwgohComlink or call private methods directly.

docs.title: Constructor inheritance
docs.text:
SwgohComlink and SwgohComlinkAsync now inherit from SwgohComlinkBase. The constructor parameters are unchanged, but the subclass signature uses **kwargs:

# Both still work:
comlink = SwgohComlink(url="http://myhost:3000")
comlink = SwgohComlink(host="myhost", port=3000)

docs.title: _request() signature
docs.text:
def _request(
      self,
      method: str = "POST",
-     url_base: str | None = None,
      endpoint: str | None = None,
      payload: dict | list | None = None,
+     stats: bool = False,
+     timeout: float | None = None,
  ) -> dict | list:
  • url_base was removed — the method now selects between self.url_base and self.stats_url_base based on the stats flag.
  • timeout allows per-request timeout overrides.

docs.title: _post() signature
docs.text: Same changes as _request() — url_base replaced by stats and timeout.

docs.title: 7. Removed sentinels
docs.text:
All sentinel objects (OPTIONAL, NotSet, REQUIRED, MISSING, GIVEN, MutualExclusiveRequired) have been removed from swgoh_comlink.helpers. Remove any sentinel imports from your code.

- from swgoh_comlink.helpers import (
-     REQUIRED,
-     MISSING,
-     GIVEN,
-     OPTIONAL,
-     NotSet,
-     MutualExclusiveRequired,
- )

Functions that previously used sentinel defaults now use standard Python patterns: required parameters have no default, and optional parameters default to None.

docs.title: 8. GAC bracket helpers
docs.text:
get_gac_brackets() and async_get_gac_brackets() have two changes:

  1. The limit parameter changed from a sentinel default to int with default 0 (where 0 means "no limit"):

    - get_gac_brackets(comlink, league="KYBER", limit=OPTIONAL)
+ get_gac_brackets(comlink, league="KYBER", limit=0)

  2. Bracket boundary discovery now uses exponential probing with binary search, reducing HTTP requests from O(n) to O(log n). The async variant also fetches brackets in parallel batches via asyncio.gather. No code changes are needed on your side — the return format is identical.

docs.title: 9. GameDataItems server alignment
docs.text:
DataItems and Constants were re-synced against the live GameDataItemsEnum that get_enums() now exposes. Two practical impacts:

Segment2 and Segment4 aggregate values changed. If you hardcoded the integers in your own code (rather than referencing the constants by name), update them:

Constant Old value New value DataItems.SEGMENT2 / Constants.Segment2 68717379584 1125968624222208 DataItems.SEGMENT4 / Constants.Segment4 281200098803712 3377424842620928

SEGMENT1 (2097151) and SEGMENT3 (206158430208) are unchanged.

Code that references the constant by name (DataItems.SEGMENT2, Constants.Segment2, Constants.get("Segment2")) picks up the new values automatically.

get_game_data(items=...) accepts any in-range bitmask. Comlink accepts any items value from 1 to 252 − 1, or -1 (DataItems.ALL) for everything, so single collections (e.g. DataItems.UNITS), custom combinations and the SEGMENT1–SEGMENT4 aggregates all work. Out-of-range values are rejected with an HTTP 400. Earlier versions of this guide advised against single-collection values; the failures behind that advice were most likely caused by a since-fixed Comlink bug in how CDN URLs were built, so upgrade Comlink if you still see them.

Combine members with | rather than +. Aliased members (e.g. CONQUEST_DEFINITION and ARTIFACT_DEFINITION, which are both the CONQUEST bit) set a different bit when added together.

New members added (from the live GameDataItemsEnum): ABILITY_DECISION_TREE, ERA_DEFINITION, UBS_UPDATE. New legacy-name aliases: AbilityDecisionTrees, EraDefinitions, UBSUpdate, EpisodeDefinitions (plural), AccountLinking.

docs.title: Summary of changes
docs.text: Area Before (v1.x) After HTTP library requests httpx Transport exception requests.RequestException SwgohComlinkException (wraps httpx.RequestError) Exception hierarchy SwgohComlinkException, SwgohComlinkValueError Added SwgohComlinkTypeError get_logger(log_level=) Accepted log_level, auto-configured handlers No log_level param, no auto-configuration Default log output Console output at INFO level Silent (NullHandler only) Client lifecycle No close needed Use with or call close() Async support Not available SwgohComlinkAsync Local stat calc Not available StatCalc (sync) / StatCalcAsync (async) _request(url_base=) url_base parameter stats bool + timeout helpers.py Single 1,970-line file helpers/ subpackage (all imports preserved) All sentinels Exported from helpers Removed — use None or required positional args get_gac_brackets(limit=) Sentinel default int default 0 (0 = no limit) GAC bracket scanning Linear O(n) Exponential probe + binary search O(log n) Migration checker Not available swgoh-migrate CLI / python -m swgoh_comlink.migrate DataItems.SEGMENT2 value 68717379584 1125968624222208 (server-aligned) DataItems.SEGMENT4 value 281200098803712 3377424842620928 (server-aligned) get_game_data(items=) values Any bitmask Any bitmask from 1 to 252 − 1, or -1; out of range → HTTP 400

docs.title: Standalone research repo, not a branch of upstream
docs.text:
Status: accepted. §Consequences line 14 ("No PRs, tags, releases, or pushes …") is superseded by ADR-0008 for PEP 440 pre-release versions distributed as GitHub Releases. All other clauses of this ADR stay in force.

v3 of swgoh_comlink is developed in a separate local clone at /Users/marktripod/code/comlink-python-v3/, decoupled from the public swgoh-utils/comlink-python repo. Once research is mature, a separate decision will be made about how (or whether) to re-incorporate changes upstream — by cherry-picking, opening a PR, forking, or abandoning.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: A worktree- or branch-based v3 inside the public repo coupled v3's experimental cadence to upstream's release cycle, blocked v3 work on unrelated v2.1-track merges (develop → main), and complicated the gitignore / topology mechanics. A standalone clone lets v3 evolve pyproject.toml, dependency floors, the package layout, even the package name without affecting upstream contributors, and removes any risk of accidentally pushing experimental commits.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• ~/code/comlink-python/ is never touched by v3 work.
  • No PRs, tags, releases, or pushes from this repo until a reintegration decision is made.
  • Pulling in upstream bug fixes (e.g. the arena-payout fixes currently on develop) is a manual git fetch upstream && git cherry-pick step rather than automatic.
  • The package keeps the name swgoh_comlink during research to minimize diff churn; renaming is a reintegration-time concern.

docs.title: Python ≥3.11 floor for v3.0
docs.text:
Status: accepted

v3.0 sets requires-python = ">=3.11", up from v2.x's >=3.10.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
3.11 adds language and stdlib features used throughout the v3 design: typing.Self for the _BaseClient.with_options(...) -> Self shape, tomllib for pyproject reads without a third-party dep, Exception.add_note for richer error messages, and a ~10–15% interpreter startup improvement that compounds with the Phase 5 lazy-import work to deliver the headline cold-import number.

Dropping 3.10-only users is acceptable for a major version, especially given that uv and pyenv make multi-version installs trivial for the bot-operator audience that consumes this library.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• _base_client.py can use Self from typing directly; no typing_extensions dependency.
  • Ruff and mypy targets move to py311.
  • The Phase 5 cold-import baseline benefits from CPython 3.11's startup work in addition to the SDK's own lazy-loading changes.
  • Users on RHEL 9 or Ubuntu 22.04's system Python (3.10 and 3.9 respectively) must install 3.11+ via uv, pyenv, or deadsnakes.

docs.title: No __getitem__ shim on Structs in v3.0
docs.text:
Status: accepted

v3.0 returns msgspec.Struct instances from every endpoint and does not add a __getitem__ deprecation shim that would let legacy v2-style player['rosterUnit'] access keep working. Two soft on-ramps from v2 dict access are provided instead:

  1. raw=True keyword on every endpoint method — bypasses Struct decoding and returns the dict-shaped JSON.
  2. compat.to_dict(struct) — explicit one-time conversion of any Struct to a dict.

docs.title: Considered options
docs.text:
• The shim with DeprecationWarning. Smoothest possible v2 → v3 transition: existing user code runs unchanged with warnings, removed in v3.2. Rejected because it defeats the type-safety win of Structs (ty/mypy can't catch typos in obj['rosterUnt'] the way they can in obj.roster_unt), it requires nontrivial camelCase ↔ snake_case mapping machinery that exposes exactly the friction users would hit, and deprecation warnings in practice get either silenced or pinned-in-config and never actually drive migration.
  • Per-Struct shims only on high-traffic types. Rejected for documentation friction — "why does Player support indexing but Metadata doesn't?" becomes a recurring support question.

docs.title: Why
docs.text: v3 is a major version and the dict → Struct migration is the load-bearing reason it exists. A shim signals we don't believe in our own change. raw=True and to_dict() already give two soft on-ramps; a third pushes past "ergonomic" into "compatibility theater."

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• The swgoh-migrate v2 → v3 rewriter (Phase 10) carries the migration burden via codemods (player['rosterUnit'] → player.roster_unit).
  • Users who depend on dict access pay a one-line cost per call (raw=True) or per object (to_dict(...)).
  • compat.py stays small: just to_dict and any genuinely lossless conversion helpers.

docs.title: Defer rate-limit and circuit-breaker work to v3.1
docs.text:
Status: accepted

v3.0 does not ship [ratelimit] or [circuitbreaker] extras, the DualRateLimiter, the bulk_get_* helpers, the purgatory-backed circuit breaker, or the recipe docs around them. These move to a v3.1-research milestone in this repo, gated on real bot-operator demand.

docs.title: Why
docs.text:
The original v3 plan's Phase 8 added significant scope — three new optional dependencies (aiometer, aiolimiter, purgatory), two new extras to document and test ([ratelimit], [circuitbreaker]), four benchmark scripts, dual sync/async limiter implementations, and recipe documentation — for unproven demand. No specific operator has asked for it; the (80, 1) / (18, 1) defaults in the original plan were inferred from comlink's documented limits, not from observed cascading-failure scenarios.

Shipping v3.0 without Phase 8 keeps the milestone tight (msgspec, lazy imports, sibling clients, GameDataCache, [cli], [cache], [pydantic]) and avoids paying for speculative breadth before the core wins are validated.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• v3.0 phase count drops from 10 to 9 (Phase 8 removed; old Phases 9, 10 renumber).
  • Operators who want concurrency control on v3.0 use vanilla asyncio.Semaphore patterns at the call site — documented as a recipe.
  • When demand materializes, v3.1 can ship the rate-limit work as a standalone release without forcing the rest of v3.0 to wait.

docs.title: Split typed and dict client surfaces across two import paths, supported by manifest-driven codegen
docs.text:
Status: accepted (v3.1-research)

swgoh_comlink ships two client surfaces at two import paths:

  • from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink — dict-default. Returns raw dict[str, Any] shapes. Byte-compatible with v2's wire surface.
  • from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink — typed-default. Returns msgspec.Struct instances (the v3 research format).

Async twins (SwgohComlinkAsync) live alongside in each module.

All four client classes (2 sync/async × 2 dict/typed) are code-generated from a single manifest (src/swgoh_comlink/_codegen/endpoints.py) via a Jinja template (templates/client.py.jinja) and generator script (generate.py). A pre-commit hook + CI step enforce make generate && git diff --exit-code to prevent drift.

docs.title: Why two surfaces
docs.text:
The original v3 design (Phase 3) made typed Structs the default and shipped raw=True as an opt-out per call. That made v3 a hard break from v2: every dict access (player["name"]) became broken under v3 unless the caller passed raw=True everywhere or wrapped with compat.to_dict().

For a standalone research repo (ADR-0001) with one caller, that cost was acceptable. For eventual reintegration with the public v2 repo, it would force every existing v2 user to rewrite their code on upgrade.

Splitting the surface restores the v2 upgrade path: existing dict-style code keeps working byte-for-byte; users who want the typed surface change one import line. The split also gives a cleaner mental model — each module's docs describe one shape, not both with conditional logic for a raw= kwarg.

docs.title: Why codegen
docs.text:
Without codegen, this split would mean four hand-maintained client classes with ~16 endpoint methods each — ~64 method bodies of near-identical code. Phase 4 explicitly noted that the existing sync/async duplication (0.98 ratio, ~125 SLOC per client) was unmanageable without a generation tool, and deferred unasync as the candidate.

Adding the dict/typed axis on top makes hand-maintenance untenable. The codegen turns four parallel clients into:

  • One manifest (one Python entry per endpoint).
  • One Jinja template (parametrized on is_async, is_typed).
  • One generator script.

Adding an endpoint = one manifest entry + regenerate. Diff size in PRs is large but mechanical (4 generated files plus the 1-line manifest change); reviewers focus on the manifest entry, not the four method bodies it implies.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives
docs.text:
Typed-default + raw=True everywhere (original v3.0 design). Forces v2 users to rewrite on upgrade. Documented as the wrong reintegration shape; we kept it for v3.0 only because v3.0 was research-only and the public repo wasn't on the roadmap.

Inheritance with a class-level _DEFAULT_RAW flag. The dict client would inherit from the typed client and flip a flag. Return-type annotations don't narrow on inheritance: both subclasses would advertise Player | dict[str, Any], defeating the type-checker win that is half the reason to split.

Pure metaclass dispatch. Same class, runtime-swapped return shape via __init_subclass__ or __getattribute__. mypy-hostile; debugging-hostile; magic that future readers wouldn't grep for.

unasync for the sync/async axis only. Standard tool, but it only addresses one of the two axes. We'd still hand-maintain dict/typed. Pure manifest-driven Jinja covers both axes from one source — simpler.

Codegen _payloads.py or _models.py. Payload builders carry validation logic; Structs carry schema specifics. Generating them would multiply the toolchain for no maintenance win. They stay hand-maintained; the manifest references them by name.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• For existing v3-research callers (internal): one-line import change (swgoh_comlink.SwgohComlink → swgoh_comlink.typed.SwgohComlink) to keep typed access. Migration guide documents this.
  • For future v2 reintegration: existing v2 callers keep working without code change. Typed access is opt-in via the new import path. This becomes the recommended upgrade pattern.
  • For maintainers: all endpoint changes happen in the manifest; the four client files are generated and marked DO NOT EDIT. A pre-commit hook enforces regeneration when the manifest changes.
  • For Phase 5's lazy-import discipline: the dict client's imports don't pull msgspec Structs at module load — only the typed client does. Cold-import time on import swgoh_comlink stays in the ~7 ms range that Phase 5 measured.
  • Escape hatches (healthcheck, raw_request, stream_game_data, stream_localization) stay hand-written in mixins (_escape_hatches_sync.py / _escape_hatches_async.py). Their bodies are non-uniform (different return shapes, no decoder dispatch, bypass retry, streaming context managers); manifest-ifying them would force conditional branches that outweigh the duplication win.
  • _payloads.py and _models.py stay the source of truth for payload shapes and Struct definitions. They're imported by name from the generated files; manifest entries reference them as strings (payload_builder="player_payload", typed_decoder="PLAYER_DECODER").

docs.title: StatCalc internals overhaul — three-axis research; ship A + E
docs.text:
Status: accepted (v3.2-research)

swgoh_comlink.StatCalc was the deferred-since-Phase-3.5 subpackage — v3 Phases 3.5, 7, 8, and 9 each considered touching it and declined ("StatCalc internals carry no v3 architectural debt — they work as-is with the new client surface."). v3.2-research revisits that decision along three orthogonal axes, with research-first / measure-then-ship discipline and pre-registered decision rules.

This ADR records what the eight candidates across three axes delivered and which two shipped.

docs.title: The three axes
docs.text: Axis Problem Candidates considered Input format StatCalc is dict-only. Typed-client users pay a msgspec.to_builtins(player) ≈ +25 % conversion tax to hand it a Player Struct. A — full to_builtins adapter at boundary. B — partial conversion (only StatCalc-read fields). C — accessor-abstraction subclass. Parallelism calc_player_stats runs serially in ~21 ms for a 397-unit roster despite being embarrassingly parallel. D — ProcessPoolExecutor with threshold-gated fan-out + worker initializer. Game-data shape GameDataBuilder._build_game_data runs ~25 ms at every process startup. _table_get is a polymorphic dispatcher called ~72k times per calc_player_stats iteration. E — persist normalized game_data via GameDataCache. F — typed-Struct game_data tables. G — direct consumption of v3.1 typed /data segments. H — hot-table index restructuring.

docs.title: Pre-registered decision rule
docs.text:
Locked in before any prototype landed (per the "research-first / measure-then-ship" discipline; the rule pre-empts post-hoc rationalization). Each candidate ships iff it clears its threshold AND parity passes byte-for-byte against the dict-baseline on every cassette.

Axis Threshold Input format dict_overhead ≤ 2 % AND struct_overhead ≤ 10 %. If no candidate clears the Struct bar, ship Candidate A (floor option) and recommend raw=True for hot paths. Parallelism parallel_speedup ≥ 2× on 397-unit roster at optimal worker count AND serial_path_regression ≤ 1 %. Game-data shape (cold-start: E) cold_start_improvement ≥ 50 %. Game-data shape (hot path: F, G, H) hot_path_improvement ≥ 10 % AND parallelism (D) regression ≤ 5 %.

F and G are mutually exclusive (F enhances GameDataBuilder; G replaces it). E and H are additive with each other and with F/G.

docs.title: Measured outcomes
docs.text: All numbers on the 397-unit player_large cassette unless noted. Baseline calc_player_stats (dict path): 22.6 ms warm.

docs.title: Input format
docs.text:
Candidate Struct overhead Dict overhead Verdict A. Full to_builtins adapter +22.9 % 0 % SHIPS (floor option) B. Partial-conversion adapter +21.4 % 0 % Defer (no win over A) C. Accessor abstraction subclass +23.6 % 0 % Defer (slightly worse than A)

Finding. The bulk of the conversion cost is msgspec.to_builtins on the per-Mod sub-Structs — all three candidates pay this cost equivalently. B's "skip Player metadata" optimization saves only ~0.3 ms; C's "interleave with calc" hypothesis added isinstance overhead that cancelled the win.

All three failed the ≤ 10 % Struct-overhead threshold. Under the floor-option rule, Candidate A ships as the cleanest minimum-viable bimorphic surface; the recipe (docs/v3/recipes/typed-statcalc.md) documents client.get_player(..., raw=True) as the zero-overhead path for hot loops.

Bug surfaced by parity testing during this work: the original audit declared RosterUnit.equipment "always empty in cassettes." False — GREATMOTHERS (a ship) carries 4 equipment pieces, and _get_crew_rating reads len(equipped) for crew rating. The prototype's partial-conversion adapter had to add equipment to match GP and final stats. Lesson recorded: parity testing is load-bearing; field-access audits lie.

docs.title: Parallelism
docs.text:
Worker count player_small (115u) player_large (397u) Serial 3.24 ms 21.59 ms 2 workers 2.78 ms (1.16×) 26.84 ms (0.80×) 4 workers 2.02 ms (1.60×) 25.40 ms (0.85×) 8 workers 2.41 ms (1.34×) 25.94 ms (0.83×)

Verdict: D does not ship. On player_large, parallel is consistently slower than serial despite a counterintuitive win on player_small. Root cause: Python ProcessPoolExecutor IPC break-even (~500 µs/task even with batching) exceeds StatCalc's per-unit work (~70 µs). The serial ship-pass tail (ships need character results first) further eats into the parallel chars-pass gain on large rosters.

D fails the ≥ 2× speedup bar AND the ≤ 1 % serial-regression bar (adding the async surface adds ~1.5 % overhead even on the sync fast-path). Deferred without ship.

docs.title: Game-data shape
docs.text:
Candidate Cold-start Hot path Verdict E. Cached normalized game_data 25.74 ms → 3.62 ms (+85.9 %) 0 % SHIPS F. Typed-Struct tables 0 % est. 1.3 % (mechanism-bound) Defer (no prototype) G. Direct typed-segment consumption est. 100 % (no rebuild) est. -5 % to +10 % Defer (no prototype) H. Hot-table index restructuring 0 % +5.7 % Defer

E ships. Cleared the ≥ 50 % cold-start threshold with margin. Cuts process startup from ~26 ms to ~4 ms by persisting the normalized form alongside the raw /data payload via GameDataCache. Major win for cron jobs, lambdas, CLI invocations.

H deferred. Targeted variant (pre-alias 7 hottest CR tables; pre-flatten the (pips, level) mod-rarity lookup; lightweight _table_get override) delivered 5.7 % — below the 10 % bar. An aggressive variant (_normalize_nested_dict_keys recursive normalization + dict-only _table_get) delivered 8-15 % but broke parity on units with mod-set bonuses (Strength 451 → 368 on GREATMOTHERS). The bug is somewhere in nested-key normalization conflicting with mixed str/int key access elsewhere in the codebase. The plan's "low effort" estimate for H did not anticipate that debugging cost.

F deferred without prototyping. A micro-bench established that msgspec Struct attribute access saves only ~3.8 ns per call vs dict.get. At 72k _table_get calls per iter, that yields ~0.28 ms savings on a 22 ms baseline = 1.3 % improvement. The plan's 10-20 % estimate was off by an order of magnitude. Mechanism-bound below threshold.

G deferred without prototyping. Higher refactor cost than F (rewrite every internal table lookup to traverse the typed /data Struct graph), with the plan's own estimated payoff range of "-5 % to +10 %" suggesting it could regress performance. The pattern of candidate overestimation across the plan + the mechanism analysis from F's micro-bench together argue G would not deliver. Effort:payoff ratio rules it out.

docs.title: What ships in v3.2
docs.text:
Two changes land on v3.2-research:

  1. Candidate A — StatCalc.calc_player_stats and StatCalc.calc_roster_stats accept either a Comlink-format dict tree OR a msgspec.Struct (single Player or list of Player, single RosterUnit list, etc.). Conversion happens once at the boundary via msgspec.to_builtins; everything downstream stays dict-only.

  2. Candidate E — from swgoh_comlink.StatCalc import get_statcalc_game_data. Drop-in helper that takes a client + a GameDataCache and returns the normalized game_data ready to hand to StatCalc(game_data=...). On cold start, builds + persists. On every subsequent process, msgpack-decodes from disk (~4 ms vs ~26 ms cold).

Parity tests live at tests/unit/test_statcalc_v3_2.py — assert byte-identical per-unit stats and GP for both shipped surfaces against the dict-baseline on every cassette.

docs.title: Rejected alternatives (explicit)
docs.text:
• Candidate B / C (partial / accessor input adapters). Don't beat A — measured. Conversion cost is dominated by per-Mod to_builtins, which all three pay. Carrying additional candidate modules for ~1 % margin would have been pure complexity.
  • Candidate D (ProcessPoolExecutor). IPC break-even exceeds per-unit work. Regresses on player_large despite winning on player_small — wrong shape for this workload. Defer until either per-unit work grows (e.g. Cython inner loops shipped) OR Python's IPC cost shrinks (sub-interpreters, free-threaded build).
  • Candidate F / G / H (game-data hot-path reshape). None cleared the 10 % hot-path bar. F's mechanism is bounded below threshold; G has higher cost than F with negative-bound payoff; H's targeted variant misses, aggressive variant breaks parity.
  • Cython / Rust / native acceleration of inner math loops. Out of scope; will revisit only when caller demand data warrants a v3.3 conversation.
  • StatCalc/ → statcalc/ PEP 8 rename. Sibling effort; doesn't interact with the bimorphic / parallelism / game-data work; cleaner to land independently.

docs.title: Process notes
docs.text:
• One integration branch (v3.2/statcalc-final-integration) lands ONLY the winning candidates. Throwaway prototype branches (v3.2/statcalc-{bimorphic-prototypes,prototype-d,prototype-efgh}) stay around for reference and do not merge.
  • Every plan estimate proved optimistic. Across Phases 2-4, none of the eight candidates exceeded its plan-stated estimate — six fell short or failed entirely. The honest pre-registered decision rules saved us from shipping things that didn't pay back.
  • Branch ordering: v3.1-research ← v3.2-research ← phase branches. v3.0-dev remains frozen per ADR-0001.

docs.title: StatCalc rewrite evaluation — three-axis research with pre-registered decision rule
docs.text:
Status: accepted (v3.3-research) — pre-registered in Phase 1; measured outcomes appended in Phase 5 before the integration commit landed. See "Phase 5 measured outcomes" below.

ADR-0006 closed v3.2 with the explicit deferral: "Cython / Rust / native acceleration of inner math loops. Out of scope; will revisit only when caller demand data warrants a v3.3 conversation." This ADR records that conversation and the decision rule that will govern which v3.3 candidates ship.

This ADR is written and committed before any prototype lands. Phase 5 appends measured outcomes; the integration commit lands only candidates that cleared their pre-registered bar.

docs.title: The three axes
docs.text: Axis Problem Candidates considered Pure-Python restructure _calculate_mod_stats is 165 lines with 11 hard-coded stat-ID branches; _table_get is a polymorphic dispatcher with a 28 % cProfile tax; _format_stats is 127 lines with 4 nested scopes; char and ship paths share no abstraction. Phase 2 — single throwaway prototype that table-drives mod stats, replaces _table_get with 6 typed accessors, decomposes _format_stats, and dedups char/ship dispatch. Native acceleration ADR-0006 deferred native code; v3.2's _calculate_mod_stats inner-kernel costs are pure Python interpretation. Phase 3a — Cython .pyx inner kernel. Phase 3b — mypyc whole-module compilation. Phase 3c — Rust/PyO3 kernel via maturin. Algorithmic / data-shape rewrite v3.2 Candidate H delivered 5.7 % targeted; aggressive variant broke parity on mod-set bonuses. v3.2 Candidate A's bimorphic path costs +22.9 % almost entirely from per-Mod msgspec.to_builtins. Phase 4a — H re-attack with parity-test-first discipline. Phase 4b — typed-fastpath reading Struct slots directly, skipping to_builtins.

docs.title: Pre-registered decision rule
docs.text:
Locked in this ADR before any v3.3 prototype is implemented. Same "research-first, measure-then-ship" discipline that ADR-0006 codified for v3.2.

Each axis has its own threshold; the three are orthogonal — each ships independently when its bar is met. Every shipped path must also pass byte-for-byte parity against the v3.2 dict baseline on every recorded cassette.

Axis Threshold Hot-path speed hot_path_improvement ≥ 10 % vs v3.2 dict baseline on calc_player_stats(player_large) warm. Memory regression ≤ 5 %. Build/distribution overhead acceptable per Phase 3 analysis. If only native variants clear 10 %, ship the cheapest distribution profile (typically mypyc < Cython < Rust). Memory footprint resident_game_data_reduction ≥ 20 % (new metric for v3.3; baseline measured in Phase 1). Hot path regression ≤ 2 %. Typed-client ergonomics bimorphic_struct_overhead ≤ 5 % (vs v3.2 +22.9 %). Bimorphic parity preserved (dict input continues to work). Replaces the v3.2 Candidate A internal dispatcher; external behaviour unchanged.

If no candidate clears its axis bar, that axis ships nothing and defers to v3.4. ADR-0007 is updated to record the measured outcome either way.

docs.title: Build / distribution as a decision-rule input
docs.text:
Native variants (Phase 3) must ship a written build/distribution analysis on their prototype branch covering:

  • Wheels matrix (5 OSes × 3 Pythons = 15 wheels per release).
  • cibuildwheel config + GitHub Actions CI cost estimate.
  • Pure-Python fallback contract — STATCALC_NO_NATIVE=1 hides the extension and the test suite asserts identical output via the fallback path.
  • Source-build path preservation — pip install swgoh-comlink from sdist must continue to succeed without a C compiler / Rust toolchain. Native build is opt-in via pip install swgoh-comlink[native].
  • CI complexity impact — v3.2 baseline is ~3 min per push; full cibuildwheel matrix is 30–60 min. Mitigation: build wheels on release-tag push only.

A native variant that clears the 10 % speed bar but adds 30-minute-per-push CI overhead loses to a pure-Python winner that also clears 10 %. This is part of the hot-path decision rule, not a soft consideration.

docs.title: Out of scope (explicit)
docs.text:
• StatCalc/ → statcalc/ PEP 8 rename. Sibling effort, doesn't interact, cleaner to land independently.
  • v3.0-dev branch (frozen per ADR-0001).
  • v3.1-research shipped surfaces (typed segments, codegen, async cache).
  • v3.2 shipped surfaces — Candidate A bimorphic + Candidate E cache must continue to work and pass their parity tests. If typed-fastpath (Phase 4b) ships, it replaces A's internal dispatcher; A's external behaviour stays.
  • Readability / maintainability as a primary metric. Cyclomatic complexity and method-length tracking are informational only.
  • Candidate D (parallelism, v3.2). Stays settled unless Phase 3 introduces a Python-version axis (3.13t free-threaded or PEP 684 sub-interpreters) that flips the IPC math. If so, re-measure D under the new mechanism.
  • Candidate G (direct typed-segment consumption, v3.2). Stays "deferred without prototyping" unless Phase 1 surfaces new information.
  • v3.2 Candidates B / C / F — measured and rejected for mechanism reasons that don't change under any v3.3 axis. Re-measure only if the mechanism itself shifts (e.g. F-tables under mypyc compilation may resurface; F-tables alone won't).

docs.title: Process
docs.text:
• Branch: v3.3-research off v3.2-research (HEAD ef7a542). v3.0-dev and v3.1-research untouched.
  • Phase 1 (v3.3/statcalc-bench-extensions) is the only phase that always merges — adds memory + ergonomics axes to the existing benchmark harness and this ADR.
  • Phases 2–4 live on throwaway prototype branches that may or may not merge. Phase 5 lands ONLY the winners on v3.3/statcalc-final-integration → --no-ff to v3.3-research.
  • Parity-test discipline carries forward from v3.2 (the GREATMOTHERS lesson: field-access audits lie; parity tests are load-bearing). Phase 4a writes the regression fixture FIRST.

docs.title: Phase 5 measured outcomes
docs.text: All measurements on the 397-unit player_large cassette, warm. v3.3 baseline (recorded against v3.2-research HEAD ef7a542): 21.80 ms for calc_player_stats(dict).

docs.title: Per-candidate results
docs.text: Candidate Branch Metric Measured Threshold Verdict Phase 2 — pure-Python restructure v3.3/statcalc-pure-python-restructure hot-path 19.90 ms (+8.7 %) ≥ 10 % Below bar alone; ships combined Phase 3a — Cython kernel + Phase 2 v3.3/statcalc-cython-prototype hot-path 17.91 ms (+17.8 %) ≥ 10 % CLEARS — DOES NOT SHIP (see below) Phase 3b — mypyc + Phase 2 v3.3/statcalc-mypyc-prototype hot-path 18.54 ms (+15.0 %) ≥ 10 % CLEARS — DOES NOT SHIP (see below) Phase 3c — Rust/PyO3 + Phase 2 v3.3/statcalc-rust-kernel-prototype hot-path est. ~+10-15 %; not measured (toolchain) ≥ 10 % Mechanism-bound below Cython; DEFER Phase 4a — H re-attack not prototyped hot-path est. ~+5-8 % alone ≥ 10 % Deferred (would clear only combined with native; rolled into Cython results above) Phase 4b — typed-fastpath v3.3/statcalc-typed-fastpath ergonomics bimorphic Struct overhead: +10.1 % (down from v3.2 +22.9 %) ≤ 5 % Below bar; SHIPS as partial-win Phase 2 + 4b integration v3.3/statcalc-final-integration hot-path 18.24 ms (+16.3 %) ≥ 10 % CLEARS — SHIPS (any) — memory game_data: 12.9 MB → 12.9 MB ≥ 20 % Nothing shipped (no candidate targeted memory)

docs.title: Surprise — game_data was much smaller than estimated
docs.text: Phase 1 baseline measured game_data resident at 12.9 MB (asizeof) — the plan had estimated 50-100 MB. The ≥ 20 % bar (target ≤ 10.3 MB) remained meaningful but the absolute win was smaller than imagined. None of the Phase 2-4 candidates targeted memory directly, so this axis ships nothing in v3.3. Documented for v3.4 consideration.

docs.title: Build/distribution cost decision (the deferred native variants)
docs.text:
All three native variants (Phase 3a/3b/3c) cleared or near-cleared the ≥ 10 % hot-path bar but all add substantial build/distribution complexity:

  • 15-wheel matrix per release (5 OSes × 3 Pythons).
  • 30-60 min cibuildwheel CI on every release tag (vs v3.2 baseline ~3 min per push).
  • Cython needs a C compiler at install time for sdist; mypyc shadows the .py source (harder to test the fallback); Rust requires rustup (not just brew install rust).
  • Pure-Python fallback path needs ongoing parity testing.

The pre-registered rule's build/distribution clause says "acceptable per Phase 3 analysis." For a small research library serving the SWGOH community, the 15-wheel matrix is not justified by the +6-9 percentage points of additional speed that Cython/mypyc deliver on top of Phase 2 alone. Native variants stay on their throwaway prototype branches as future options if production demand grows.

The integration commit combines Phase 2 + Phase 4b, delivering +16.3 % on the hot path (Phase 2 alone was 8.7 %; combined with Phase 4b's calc_roster_stats simplification on the bimorphic boundary, the dict path additionally benefits from removed [to_builtins(u) for u in units] overhead even though that path is logically only exercised by Struct callers).

docs.title: Lessons (carried forward to v3.4)
docs.text:
• Pure-Python wins were larger than expected when combined across multiple targeted changes. Phase 2 alone (~9 %), Phase 2
  • Phase 4b (~16 %). Compounding effects are real.
  • Native acceleration's mechanism-bound ceiling is lower than plan estimates. Cython delivered 17.8 % (close to the upper band of the plan's 5-15 % range); mypyc 15.0 % (mid-range). PyO3 mechanism analysis ruled out higher gain (per-call boundary cost dominates on this workload's call granularity). Confirms the plan's "wins only if the kernel is hot enough" guidance.
  • Equipment field surprise (Phase 4b): initial attempt replaced equipment with [None] * len(...) thinking only the length mattered. _get_char_raw_stats actually reads each entry's equipmentId for gear stat lookup. Tests caught it immediately. Recorded as another "field-access audits lie; parity testing is load-bearing" data point. v3.2's GREATMOTHERS lesson keeps paying.
  • mypyc has worse fallback-testing ergonomics than Cython. mypyc compiles in place and shadows the .py source — there's no STATCALC_NO_NATIVE equivalent. For parity-test discipline this matters: Cython's explicit _kernel.pyx + _kernel_native.py wrapper is the better authoring pattern even though mypyc has cleaner write-time ergonomics.
  • Brew Rust is x86_64-only on Apple Silicon without rustup — worth documenting if v3.4 ever revisits native code, because it's a real installation papercut for contributors.

docs.title: What ships in v3.3
docs.text:
Two changes land on v3.3-research:

  1. Phase 2 — pure-Python restructure of StatCalc internals. Three parts: lightweight _table_get (drop the dead list-path branch), table-driven _calculate_mod_stats via the new _mod_stat_rules module (165 lines → 5), eliminated 10 per-call lambdas in _format_stats. Cleaner code AND ~9 % faster.

  2. Phase 4b — typed-fastpath for bimorphic Struct input. New _typed_fastpath module reads msgspec.Struct.__slots__ directly instead of calling msgspec.to_builtins. Bimorphic overhead drops from v3.2's +22.9 % to +10.1 %. Doesn't clear the aggressive ≤ 5 % bar but is a meaningful caller-facing improvement that ships under the partial-win clause.

Combined integration measured at +16.3 % on player_large warm (21.80 ms → 18.24 ms), well above the ≥ 10 % bar.

Parity tests at tests/unit/test_statcalc_v3_3_parity.py + tests/unit/test_statcalc_v3_2.py — 12 tests; byte-identical per-unit stats + GP on every cassette.

docs.title: Pre-release distribution via GitHub Releases (alpha / beta / rc)
docs.text:
Status: accepted (2026-05-19). Supersedes ADR-0001 §"Consequences" line 14 ("No PRs, tags, releases, or pushes from this repo until a reintegration decision is made") only for PEP 440 pre-release versions distributed as GitHub Releases. All other clauses of ADR-0001 stay in force.

v3 has shipped four research phases (v3.0 through v3.3) with full parity tests, async-aware client surfaces, typed /data segments, GameDataCache, bimorphic StatCalc, and a pure-Python restructure delivering +16.3 % on the hot path. 888 tests pass on the integration branch. The work is far enough along that community early adopters can usefully install + report bugs.

ADR-0001's "no tags or releases" clause was written when v3's surface was unstable and a pre-release would have been irresponsible. That condition no longer holds for the v3.0.0 series of alpha releases. But the bigger ADR-0001 decision — whether and how to reintegrate with upstream — is a separate, larger conversation that we are not yet ready to have. This ADR carves a narrow exception so we can ship something tryable without prejudging the reintegration question.

docs.title: Decision
docs.text:
Permitted under this ADR:

  • PEP 440 pre-release versions (aN, bN, rcN) tagged on this repo, distributed as GitHub Releases only. The wheel + sdist are attached as Release assets; the canonical install instructions are pip install <github-release-url-to-wheel> or pip install git+https://...@v3.0.0aN.
  • A new workflow .github/workflows/alpha-release.yml that builds, signs (Sigstore keyless OIDC), and creates the GitHub Release.
  • An auxiliary .github/labels.yml + label-sync workflow that manages the v2 / v3 issue labels so triagers can disambiguate bug reports.

Forbidden under this ADR:

  • Any push to PyPI from this repo. The existing .github/workflows/release.yml (which targets PyPI via OIDC trusted publishing) is not triggered by this exception. PyPI publication remains gated on reintegration with upstream.
  • Any non-pre-release tag (3.0.0, 3.0.1, 3.1.0, …). Final releases on this repo would commit to a successor relationship with upstream that this ADR explicitly does not establish.
  • Tagging directly on a research branch. Pre-release tags MUST originate from a release/v* branch cut from the relevant research branch (or main); the alpha-release workflow enforces this with a branch-ref guard.

Stability ladder for pre-releases under this ADR:

Channel Stability commitment aN (alpha) None. API may change without warning between aN and a(N+1). Use for evaluation and bug reporting only. bN (beta) Aspirational. Breaking changes possible but the maintainer commits to documenting them in the release notes. rcN (release candidate) Full. Breaking changes only for security fixes; otherwise treat as the final release surface.

If the maintainer wants to ship a final 3.0.0 (no aN/bN/rcN suffix), that requires either (a) reintegration with upstream and publishing through .github/workflows/release.yml to PyPI, or (b) a new ADR that supersedes this one and explicitly permits final releases from the research repo.

docs.title: Addendum: fork-hosted distribution (2026-07-12)
docs.text:
This ADR originally assumed pre-release tags and GitHub Releases would live on this repo's origin (swgoh-utils/comlink-python). Pushing a release/v* branch, tag, and Release to the upstream org's repo is reintegration-adjacent in a way ADR-0001 flags as a separate decision. To keep the upstream repo fully untouched, v3 pre-releases are hosted on the maintainer fork MarTrepodi/comlink-python instead:

  • The release/v* branch is pushed to the fork; alpha-release.yml runs there and creates the tag + prerelease GitHub Release on the fork.
  • All install URLs (README, CHANGELOG, release notes, wheel metadata project.urls) point at the fork for the duration of the alpha channel.
  • On reintegration, hosting moves back per the sunset clause and the URLs revert to swgoh-utils/comlink-python.

Everything else in this ADR (permitted/forbidden actions, stability ladder, sunset) is unchanged; "this repo" in the clauses above now reads as "the fork" for distribution purposes, while the PyPI and final-tag prohibitions apply to both repos.

docs.title: Sunset
docs.text:
This ADR's exception expires when whichever first occurs:

  1. Reintegration with upstream completes (at which point release.yml takes over and this exception is moot), OR
  2. 2027-05-19 (twelve months from acceptance). At that point a new ADR re-evaluates whether the pre-release channel has met its goals or should be retired.

If neither occurs by the sunset date, alpha distribution must pause pending an ADR review.

docs.title: Consequences
docs.text:
• Community early adopters can install + report bugs against v3.0.0aN without waiting for reintegration. ADR-0001's intent (no surprise upstream contamination) is preserved because PyPI remains untouched and the swgoh_comlink PyPI namespace continues to point at v2.x.
  • A v3 GitHub issue label (synced from .github/labels.yml) disambiguates v3-alpha bug reports from v2-stable bug reports. The bug-report and feature-request issue templates require a Version dropdown so triagers can filter cleanly.
  • The release branch convention (release/v* cut from a research branch, tagged via the alpha-release workflow, then merged back to the source research branch with a chore(release): resume dev cycle at <next>.dev0 commit) is now the established pattern for any pre-release this repo cuts.

docs.title: Alternatives considered + rejected
docs.text:
• Rename to swgoh-comlink-next and publish to PyPI. Breaks the succession path to v2's PyPI name; eventual reintegration would require a second rename. Rejected.
  • Publish to PyPI under --pre (still as swgoh_comlink). Irreversible in the namespace sense — once a pre-release ships to PyPI under the v2 package name, the maintainer relationship to upstream is implicitly redefined. Narrows escape hatches. Rejected.
  • Private TestPyPI distribution. Adds install friction for community testers (custom --index-url). The audience for this alpha is broader than the kind of testers who would tolerate that. Rejected.
  • Keep ADR-0001 unchanged and ship as "unofficial" artifacts outside any release process. Loses the discoverability, signing, and bug-report-channel benefits of GitHub Releases. Rejected.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkAsync API
docs.text: SwgohComlinkAsync provides the same API as SwgohComlink with async/await support. All public methods have identical signatures — just add await to each call.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlinkAsync

async with SwgohComlinkAsync() as comlink:
    player = await comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
    guild = await comlink.get_guild(guild_id=player["guildId"])

Without a context manager, call aclose() when done:

comlink = SwgohComlinkAsync()
try:
    player = await comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
finally:
    await comlink.aclose()

docs.title: Connecting to Comlink
docs.text:
SwgohComlinkAsync takes the same constructor arguments as the synchronous client: url or host/port to choose the service, and access_key/ secret_key (or the ACCESS_KEY/SECRET_KEY environment variables) for HMAC signing. See Connecting to Comlink.

async with SwgohComlinkAsync(host="192.168.1.10", port=3000) as comlink:
    ...

docs.title: Handling Errors
docs.text: Failed calls raise the same typed HTTP errors as the synchronous client.

docs.title: Retries and Pacing
docs.text:
The retry argument takes the same RetryPolicy as the synchronous client. Waits use asyncio.sleep, so they do not block the event loop. Pacing and the hold after a rate refusal apply across concurrent tasks on one client, and the tasks start in the order they asked. A task cancelled while it waits gives its slot back, so cancelling a batch does not delay the calls that follow it:

import asyncio

from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy, SwgohComlinkAsync

async with SwgohComlinkAsync(retry=RetryPolicy(min_interval=0.4)) as comlink:
    players = await asyncio.gather(*(comlink.get_player(allycode=code) for code in allycodes))

docs.title: Stat Calculation
docs.text:
For local stat calculation in async code, use StatCalcAsync which fetches game data without blocking the event loop:

from swgoh_comlink import StatCalcAsync, SwgohComlinkAsync

async with SwgohComlinkAsync() as comlink:
    calc = await StatCalcAsync.create()
    player = await comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
    calc.calc_roster_stats(player["rosterUnit"])

See the StatCalc API for full details.

docs.title: SwgohComlink API
docs.text: SwgohComlink is the synchronous client for a running swgoh-comlink service. Each method sends one request and returns the decoded JSON response. For async/await code, use SwgohComlinkAsync, which has the same methods and constructor arguments.

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink

with SwgohComlink() as comlink:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
    guild = comlink.get_guild(guild_id=player["guildId"])

Without a context manager, call close() when done:

comlink = SwgohComlink()
try:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
finally:
    comlink.close()

docs.title: Connecting to Comlink
docs.text:
The client connects to http://localhost:3000 by default. Point it at another service with either a full url, or a host and port:

comlink = SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.example.com:3000")
comlink = SwgohComlink(host="192.168.1.10", port=3000)

When host is given, url and stats_url are ignored.

If your comlink service requires HMAC signing, pass access_key and secret_key. When they are not passed, the client reads them from the ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY environment variables. Signing is turned on only when both keys are set.

See the API Reference below for every constructor argument.

docs.title: Handling Errors
docs.text: When comlink answers with an HTTP error status, the client raises a typed HTTP error, such as SwgohComlinkRateLimitError for a rate refusal or SwgohComlinkClientError for a rejected request. All of them subclass SwgohComlinkException.

docs.title: Retries and Pacing
docs.text:
By default a client makes exactly one attempt per call and raises the typed HTTP error on failure. Pass a RetryPolicy as the keyword-only retry argument to retry the failures that mean the call was not carried out:

  • rate refusals (SwgohComlinkRateLimitError: HTTP 429, or the game's Rate exceeded!)
  • HTTP 503 (SwgohComlinkUnavailableError)

Before each retry the client waits for the Retry-After header when the response has one (capped at max_retry_after), otherwise for the next value of backoff (5, 10, 20 and 40 seconds by default), plus a random extra of up to jitter times that wait (20% by default) so that calls refused together do not all retry at once. Jitter only adds time: no retry starts before the backoff or Retry-After wait. Other errors are raised at once.

A rate refusal also holds back the endpoint it came from. Until the retry wait has passed, no call to that endpoint starts on the client, whether it is a retry or a new call, so concurrent callers back off together rather than adding to the refusal. Endpoints listed in unpaced_endpoints are never held.

min_interval also spaces calls to the same endpoint. The game refuses calls with Rate exceeded! at roughly 15 calls a second per RPC on one session, so 0.4 seconds keeps a burst well under that limit.

from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy, SwgohComlink

comlink = SwgohComlink(retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=3, min_interval=0.4))
player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)

SwgohComlinkAsync accepts the same argument; see its retries section for how waits behave with concurrent tasks.

docs.title: RetryPolicy dataclass
docs.text:
How a client retries refused calls and paces calls to the same endpoint.

Pass an instance as the retry keyword argument of SwgohComlink or SwgohComlinkAsync. Without one (the default) the clients make exactly one attempt per call and never wait.

Only two failures are retried, both of which mean the call was not carried out: rate refusals (:class:~swgoh_comlink.exceptions.SwgohComlinkRateLimitError) and HTTP 503 (:class:~swgoh_comlink.exceptions.SwgohComlinkUnavailableError). Client errors, other server errors and transport failures are raised at once.

The game meters calls per session and per RPC, and refuses with Rate exceeded! at roughly 15 calls a second to one RPC. A min_interval of 0.4 s keeps a burst to one endpoint well under that.

A rate refusal also holds back the endpoint it came from: until the retry wait has passed, no call to that endpoint starts on the client, so concurrent callers back off together instead of adding to the refusal. Each retry then waits a random extra of up to jitter times its wait, so callers refused together do not all retry at the same moment.

Attributes:

Name Type Description attempts int

Total attempts per call, including the first. 1 disables retrying while keeping pacing. [Default: 5]

backoff tuple[float, ...]

Seconds to wait before each retry when the response has no usable Retry-After; the last value repeats once the schedule runs out. An empty schedule retries at once, without waiting. [Default: (5.0, 10.0, 20.0, 40.0)]

respect_retry_after bool

Wait for the server's Retry-After instead of the backoff value when the header is present. [Default: True]

max_retry_after float

Upper bound, in seconds, on a Retry-After wait. [Default: 60.0]

retry_rate_limited bool

Retry rate refusals. [Default: True]

retry_unavailable bool

Retry HTTP 503 responses. [Default: True]

min_interval float

Minimum seconds between the starts of two calls to the same endpoint on one client, across threads or tasks. 0 disables pacing. [Default: 0.0]

unpaced_endpoints frozenset[str]

Endpoint names (such as "player") exempt from min_interval and from being held back after a rate refusal. [Default: empty]

jitter float

Largest random extra added to a retry wait, as a fraction of that wait: 0.2 turns a 5 s wait into 5 to 6 s. Extra time only, so a retry never starts before the backoff or Retry-After wait. 0 disables it. [Default: 0.2]

Raises:

Type Description SwgohComlinkValueError

If a numeric field is negative, non-finite, or attempts is less than 1.

SwgohComlinkTypeError

If attempts is not an integer, a numeric field is not an int or float (bool included), backoff or unpaced_endpoints is a string or not iterable, or an endpoint name is not a string.

Examples:

Retry rate refusals and 503s, and space calls to one endpoint 0.4 s apart:

>>> from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, RetryPolicy
>>> comlink = SwgohComlink(retry=RetryPolicy(min_interval=0.4))

docs.title: retry_delay(error, attempt)
docs.text:
Return how long to wait before retrying a failed attempt, or None to give up.

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default error SwgohComlinkHTTPError

The exception raised by the attempt that failed.

required attempt int

The 1-based number of the attempt that failed.

required

Returns:

Type Description float | None

Seconds to wait before the next attempt, or None when the error is

float | None

not retryable or no attempts remain.

Examples:

>>> import httpx
>>> from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import SwgohComlinkHTTPError
>>> error = SwgohComlinkHTTPError.from_response(httpx.Response(429))
>>> RetryPolicy().retry_delay(error, attempt=1)
5.0
>>> RetryPolicy(attempts=1).retry_delay(error, attempt=1) is None
True

docs.title: jitter_extra(delay)
docs.text: Return a random extra, from 0 up to jitter * delay seconds, to add to a retry wait.

docs.title: Stat Calculation
docs.text:
To add stats and Galactic Power to the units in a player profile, pass the roster to StatCalc, which runs the calculation locally:

from swgoh_comlink import StatCalc, SwgohComlink

with SwgohComlink() as comlink:
    calc = StatCalc()
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=245866537)
    calc.calc_roster_stats(player["rosterUnit"])

See the StatCalc API for full details.

docs.title: Exceptions
docs.text:
All custom exceptions raised by swgoh_comlink inherit from SwgohComlinkException. Catching this base class is sufficient to handle any error from the library.

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import SwgohComlinkException, SwgohComlinkValueError, SwgohComlinkTypeError

comlink = SwgohComlink()

try:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=123)
except SwgohComlinkValueError:
    print("Invalid allycode format")
except SwgohComlinkTypeError:
    print("Invalid argument type")
except SwgohComlinkException:
    print("Comlink request failed")

docs.title: HTTP errors
docs.text:
When comlink answers with an HTTP error status, the clients raise a SwgohComlinkHTTPError (or one of its subclasses) from the original httpx.HTTPStatusError. str(exc) is "HTTP {status}: {body}", as it has always been, so existing handlers that catch SwgohComlinkException keep working.

Exception Raised for SwgohComlinkRateLimitError HTTP 429, or the game's Rate exceeded! refusal (sent as HTTP 502) SwgohComlinkUnavailableError HTTP 503, comlink busy or not ready SwgohComlinkClientError Any other 4xx, the request was rejected SwgohComlinkHTTPError Any other error status (5xx)

Each one has these attributes:

  • status: the HTTP status code.
  • code and detail: the code and message fields of comlink's JSON error body (detail is the raw body text when the body is not JSON).
  • retry_after: the Retry-After header in seconds, or None.
  • response: the httpx.Response.

Game error codes look like GAME_<n>, and the number can differ between calls that fail for the same reason. Match on the exception class, not on code.

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import (
    SwgohComlinkClientError,
    SwgohComlinkHTTPError,
    SwgohComlinkRateLimitError,
)

comlink = SwgohComlink()

try:
    player = comlink.get_player(allycode=123456789)
except SwgohComlinkRateLimitError as exc:
    print(f"Rate limited, retry in {exc.retry_after or 5} s")
except SwgohComlinkClientError as exc:
    print(f"Rejected ({exc.status} {exc.code}): {exc.detail}")
except SwgohComlinkHTTPError as exc:
    print(f"Comlink error {exc.status}")

To have the client retry rate refusals and 503 responses for you, pass a RetryPolicy.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkException
docs.text:
Bases: Exception

Base class for exceptions in this module.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkValueError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkException, ValueError

Raised when an argument value is invalid.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkTypeError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkException, TypeError

Raised when an argument type is invalid.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkHTTPError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkException

Raised when the comlink service answers with an HTTP error status.

str(exc) is always "HTTP {status}: {body}", and the exception is raised from the originating httpx.HTTPStatusError, so code that matched on the message or on SwgohComlinkException keeps working. Use :meth:from_response to build the most specific subclass for a response.

Attributes:

Name Type Description status

The HTTP status code.

code

The code field of a JSON error body, when present. comlink error bodies have the shape {"code": ..., "message": ...}. Codes of the form GAME_<n> vary between calls for the same failure, so match on the exception class rather than on them.

detail

The message field of a JSON error body, or the raw body text when the body is not a JSON object. None when the body is empty.

retry_after

Seconds the server asked the caller to wait, parsed from the Retry-After header (delta-seconds or HTTP-date form). None when the header is absent or unreadable. The value is not clamped.

response

The httpx.Response that carried the error, if available.

docs.title: from_response(response) classmethod
docs.text:
Build the most specific HTTP error for an error response.

Classification, first match wins:

  1. :class:SwgohComlinkRateLimitError: HTTP 429, a RATE_LIMITED code, or a message containing "Rate exceeded" (the game's own refusal, which comlink passes through as HTTP 502).
  2. :class:SwgohComlinkUnavailableError: HTTP 503.
  3. :class:SwgohComlinkClientError: any other 4xx status.
  4. :class:SwgohComlinkHTTPError: everything else (5xx).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default response Response

The error response returned by httpx.

required

Returns:

Type Description SwgohComlinkHTTPError

An instance of the matching exception class. It is not raised.

Examples:

>>> import httpx
>>> err = SwgohComlinkHTTPError.from_response(
...     httpx.Response(502, json={"code": "GAME_6", "message": "Rate exceeded!"})
... )
>>> type(err).__name__, err.status, err.code, err.detail
('SwgohComlinkRateLimitError', 502, 'GAME_6', 'Rate exceeded!')

docs.title: SwgohComlinkRateLimitError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkHTTPError

Raised when a request was refused for exceeding a rate limit.

Covers HTTP 429 from comlink and the game's own Rate exceeded! refusal, which arrives as HTTP 502. In both cases the call was not carried out, so re-issuing it after a pause is safe.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkUnavailableError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkHTTPError

Raised on HTTP 503: comlink is busy or not ready and asks to be retried.

comlink usually sends a short Retry-After with this status.

docs.title: SwgohComlinkClientError
docs.text:
Bases: SwgohComlinkHTTPError

Raised on a 4xx status other than 429: the request itself was rejected.

Retrying the same request will not succeed.

docs.title: Helpers API
docs.text:
The swgoh_comlink.helpers subpackage provides utility functions, constants, and data structures for working with game data returned by the Comlink API.

All public names are importable directly from swgoh_comlink.helpers:

from swgoh_comlink.helpers import DataItems, Constants, sanitize_allycode

docs.title: Sync and async clients
docs.text:
Helpers that make requests take a client as their first argument. Each one has an async_ twin, and the sync-named helper also accepts a SwgohComlinkAsync: it hands the call to the twin and returns an awaitable. Subclasses of either client are accepted too.

members = get_guild_members(comlink, allycode=123456789)                # SwgohComlink
members = await get_guild_members(async_comlink, allycode=123456789)    # SwgohComlinkAsync
members = await async_get_guild_members(async_comlink, allycode=123456789)

Given an async client, argument errors are raised when the result is awaited rather than when the helper is called. The async_ twins accept only async clients.

docs.title: DataItems
docs.text:
DataItems is an IntFlag enum mapping game data collection names to bit positions for use with get_game_data(items=...).

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.helpers import DataItems

comlink = SwgohComlink()

# A single collection
units = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.UNITS)

# Only the collections you need, combined with `|`
data = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.SKILL | DataItems.EQUIPMENT)

# Whole segments (the collections returned by the legacy request_segment= calls)
segments = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.SEGMENT1 | DataItems.SEGMENT2)

# All collections
everything = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.ALL)

Request only the collections you need where you can. Comlink assembles the whole response before sending it, so smaller masks are faster and use less memory on both sides. For example, DataItems.CHALLENGE | DataItems.CONQUEST returns about 32 MB in about 2.4 seconds, versus about 147 MB in about 12.5 seconds for SEGMENT2 | SEGMENT4.

Combine members with |, not +

Some members are aliases that share a bit with another member. For example, CONQUEST_DEFINITION, ARTIFACT_DEFINITION and CONQUEST_MISSION are all the CONQUEST bit. Adding aliases together sets a different bit: DataItems.CONQUEST_DEFINITION + DataItems.ARTIFACT_DEFINITION requests ABILITY_DECISION_TREE. Bitwise OR (|) is always safe.

Note

Comlink accepts any items bitmask from 1 to 252 − 1, or -1 (DataItems.ALL) for everything, and rejects values outside that range with an HTTP 400. Older Comlink releases had a bug in how CDN URLs were built that could make some single-collection requests fail; upgrade Comlink if you see that.

Use DataItems.members() to list all available member names.

docs.title: DataItems
docs.text:
Bases: IntFlag

Integer flag enum class mapping game data collection names to the integer values of their bit positions for use in the items parameter of the get_game_data() method.

Members can be combined with the bitwise OR operator (|) to request more than one collection in a single call. Requesting only the collections you need is significantly faster and uses less memory than requesting whole segments.

Examples:

units = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.UNITS) skill_equipment = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.SKILL | DataItems.EQUIPMENT) units_no_pve = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.UNITS, include_pve_units=False) segments_1_and_2 = comlink.get_game_data(items=DataItems.SEGMENT1 | DataItems.SEGMENT2)

Note

Combine members with |, not +. Aliased members share a bit, so adding them sets a different bit: DataItems.CONQUEST_DEFINITION + DataItems.ARTIFACT_DEFINITION requests ABILITY_DECISION_TREE, while DataItems.CONQUEST_DEFINITION | DataItems.ARTIFACT_DEFINITION correctly requests CONQUEST.

Comlink accepts any bitmask from 1 to 2**52 - 1, or -1 (DataItems.ALL) for everything. Values outside that range are rejected with an HTTP 400.

Some of the DataItems members are actually aliases for other members. For example, the TABLE member is an alias for the XP_TABLE member. This is done because both members name the same bit, which Comlink calls AllTables: requesting it returns two collections, xpTable and table (the latter holds lookup tables such as relic_promotion_table).

Other members are provided as a convenience. For example, the SEGMENT1 member is assigned the integer value of all the collections that are included when using the original (request_segment=) style of calling the get_game_data() method.

To retrieve all of the available game data, use the DataItems.ALL member.

A list of the member names of the DataItems class can be retrieved using the DataItems.members() class method.

docs.title: Wire Value Helpers
docs.text:
Comlink payloads are loosely typed. These functions read one raw field each and fail soft to a fixed default, so one unusable field never costs the whole record. They do not need a comlink instance.

Payload quirk Helper int64 values arrive as strings ("1655938556") as_int Ids such as matchId sometimes arrive as integers as_id Enums arrive as an int, a numeric string, the member name, or a decoder-style name such as CURRENCYTYPE_SHARDCURRENCY parse_enum, as_scalar Timestamps are seconds (guildJoinTime, Conquest lastRefreshTime) or milliseconds (lastActivityTime), and 0 means "no time" as_epoch A repeated field with one element can decode as a single object as_list Unit identifiers are "BASEID:SEVEN_STAR" or a bare "BASEID" base_id 
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink.helpers import as_epoch, as_int, base_id, parse_enum

comlink = SwgohComlink()
player = comlink.get_player(allycode=123456789)
last_active = as_epoch(player["lastActivityTime"])  # aware UTC datetime, or None
season_score = as_int(player.get("lifetimeSeasonScore"))
roster = {base_id(unit["definitionId"]) for unit in player["rosterUnit"]}

currency = comlink.get_enums()["CurrencyType"]
parse_enum(16, currency)                            # 'SHARD_CURRENCY'
parse_enum("CURRENCYTYPE_SHARDCURRENCY", currency)  # 'SHARD_CURRENCY'

Note

bool is never read as a number: as_int(True) is 0, not 1, and parse_enum(True, ...) is None. Values below 1011 are read as seconds by as_epoch (1011 seconds is the year 5138).

docs.title: as_int(value, default=0)
docs.text:
Read a payload number, which arrives as a string as often as an int.

int64 fields are quoted under proto3's JSON mapping ("1655938556") and bare elsewhere, so both parse. bool is never read as a number even though it subclasses int: int(True) is 1, which would look like real data (a score, a timestamp).

Parameters:

Name Type Description Default value Any

The raw payload value.

required default int

Returned when value is missing or is not a whole number. [Default: 0]

0

Returns:

Type Description int

The value as an int. A float is truncated; a string must hold a whole number

int

("1.5" returns default).

Examples:

>>> as_int("1655938556")
1655938556
>>> as_int(None)
0
>>> as_int("", default=-1)
-1
>>> as_int(True)
0

Parameters:
