    ├── long-running-bot.md
    ├── bulk-analyst.md
    ├── cli-script.md
    └── operator-side-concurrency.md

docs.title: How to read the phase reports
docs.text:
Each phase exit produces phase-N-report.md capturing:

  1. Scope delivered — which plan tasks landed, which were deferred.
  2. Commit SHAs — the squashed or merged set on v3.0-dev.
  3. Files touched — git diff --stat between the phase start and end.
  4. Deviations from the plan — anything in the implementation that didn't match v3_implementation_plan.md, with the why.
  5. Open questions — to-dos / risks visible at phase exit.
  6. Benchmark deltas vs baseline — table of headline metrics, raw deltas, and (where required) statistical significance.

Use phase-0-report.md as the template for later phases — the structure should stay stable so cross-phase comparisons are easy.

docs.title: Reading benchmark results
docs.text:
Raw JSON lives at benchmarks/v3/results/phase-N-*.json. Phase reports summarize; the JSON is the source of truth.

Compare any two phases with::

jq '.results[] | {metric, value, unit, status}' benchmarks/v3/results/phase-0-baseline.json

docs.title: v3 Benchmark Report
docs.text:
Consolidated v2.0.x baseline vs v3.0 final numbers across every phase. Raw JSON results live in benchmarks/v3/results/; this document is the human-readable summary.

All numbers measured on the same machine: macOS aarch64, Python 3.11.15 (uv-managed), 16-inch MacBook Pro M-series. Same comlink cassettes (recorded Phase 0) used as inputs throughout. Timings are medians of N=10–50 iterations depending on the bench; cold-import numbers are particularly noisy on a working laptop (documented in the Phase 0/1 reports' "open questions" sections — variance can be 30–50% run-to-run from system load).

docs.title: Headlines
docs.text: Metric v2.0.x baseline v3.0 final Δ Cold import swgoh_comlink 65.4 ms ~7 ms 9.3× faster (Phase 5) httpx loaded on import True False (Phase 5) get_player decode speed (large roster) 1× (json baseline) 2.67× faster (Phase 3.5) get_player decode peak memory 1× 1.83× lower (Phase 3.5) get_player object size 1× 30% smaller (Phase 3.5) GameDataCache warm path (same instance) n/a 10⁷× faster than cold (Phase 7) Method-body duplication ratio (sync/async) 1.0 0.98 (essentially 1.0) unchanged by design (Phase 4) Endpoint method total SLOC per client 125 89 −29% (Phase 4) Coverage gate (fail_under) 40 95 (Phase 9) Test count (full suite) 654 742+ new tests for every phase

docs.title: Per-metric breakdown vs Phase 0 baseline
docs.text: Cassette: see benchmarks/v3/fixtures/. Tagged data ≈ 380 MiB JSON; player_large ≈ 3.6 MiB JSON (397 units); player_small ≈ 58 KiB (115 units); others smaller.

docs.title: Phase 0 baseline (recorded against v2.0.x code at SHA cb8a512)
docs.text:
Source: benchmarks/v3/results/phase-0-baseline.json.

Metric Value cold_import_time 65.4 ms httpx_loaded_on_import True method_body_duplication_ratio 1.0 (16/16 paired methods) get_player_small_e2e_latency 0.29 ms (115-unit roster) get_player_large_e2e_latency 40.1 ms (397-unit roster) get_data_decode_time (json) 7,120 ms get_data_decode_peak_memory 1,392 MiB get_data_object_size 1,034 MiB

docs.title: Phase 2 — Resilience layer
docs.text:
bench_retry_overhead: −1.10 % overhead with max_retries=3 vs 0 on the happy path (target <2 %).

bench_retry_recovery: 429 + Retry-After: 1 → 200 takes 1.011 s wall (expected ~1.0 s). 503 (no header) → exp-jitter wait ≈ 0.35 s.

docs.title: Phase 3 + 3.5 — msgspec.Struct typing
docs.text:
Best-case wins on player_large after Phase 3.5 deep typing:

Bench v2 (json) v3 typed win bench_decode_speed (player_large) 16.8 ms 6.3 ms 2.67× faster bench_decode_speed (player_small) 0.18 ms 0.07 ms 2.49× faster bench_decode_memory (player_large peak) 17.7 MiB 9.7 MiB 1.83× lower bench_decode_memory (player_small peak) 0.31 MiB 0.13 MiB 2.45× lower bench_object_size (player_large resident) 14.4 MiB 10.0 MiB 1.43× smaller bench_object_size (player_small resident) 0.25 MiB 0.13 MiB 1.94× smaller

Plan's original projection was 3–5× faster + 4–6× lower memory + 40–60% smaller object size. Phase 3.5 closed most of the gap; the remaining shortfall is from fields still typed as dict[str, Any] (uniformly empty/null in the cassettes — equipment, unit_stat, Mod.converted_item).

/data decode speed: 1.00× (no improvement). Documented in phase-3 report as the partial-typing tradeoff — /data segments aren't deeply typed (deferred to Phase 7's GameDataCache and beyond). Object size for /data actually worsens 9% with msgspec untyped — msgspec's dict graph is marginally heavier than json.loads in this specific case.

docs.title: Phase 4 — SLOC reduction
docs.text:
Endpoint method bodies per client: 125 → 89 SLOC (-29%). Biggest methods:

Method v2 v3 get_leaderboard 19 4 get_guild 10 6 get_localization 9 4 get_game_metadata 8 3

Duplication ratio (sync vs async, post-await-stripping) stays at 0.98 (≈1.0). Achieving <10% per the plan requires code generation (unasync-style); deferred. See Phase 4 report for the analysis.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Lazy imports
docs.text:
Metric v2 v3 cold_import_time 65.4 ms 7.0 ms (9.3× reduction) httpx_loaded_on_import True False import_then_construct (first SDK call) n/a ~80 ms (deferred cost paid on first construct)

import swgoh_comlink no longer pulls httpx, msgspec, or StatCalc. PEP 562 __getattr__ resolves + caches names on first access.

docs.title: Phase 6 — Extras taxonomy
docs.text: No perf benchmarks. Test counts: +7 (test_optional.py).

docs.title: Phase 7 — GameDataCache
docs.text:
Path Time vs cold Cold (fresh on-disk cache; full pipeline) 3,549 ms 1× Disk-warm (new GameDataCache per call) 3,503 ms ~1× In-memory warm (same instance, hot loop) 0.0003 ms 10,659,556×

The plan's 100–1000× target is met on the realistic operator path (one cache instance per process). The disk-only warm path is bound by the cost of constructing 11k+ Python dicts — msgspec.msgpack vs msgspec.json doesn't matter when structure dominates.

docs.title: Phase 8 — Ergonomics
docs.text: No perf benchmarks. Test counts: +18 (test_ergonomics.py covering healthcheck, raw_request, stream_game_data, stream_localization on both sync and async clients).

docs.title: Phase 9 — Migration tooling + docs
docs.text: Deliverable What docs/v3/migration.md Side-by-side v2 → v3 examples docs/v3/recipes/*.md 4 recipes (long-running bot, bulk analyst, CLI script, operator-side concurrency) swgoh-migrate v2→v3 rules 5 new rules (V3001–V3005) in _rules.py Coverage ratchet 92 → 95 (current actual ~96.5%) bench_v3_final.py Re-runs the headline benches; produces consolidated JSON

docs.title: v3.1 — typed /data segment coverage
docs.text:
Runs on v3.1-research (not v3.0-dev — v3.0 surface is frozen per Phase 9 / ADR-0004). Hand-types 14 of /data's ~80 segments and measures dict-vs-typed decode for each. Helper: swgoh_comlink.compat.decode_segment (single generic entry point, no per-segment wrappers).

Bench: benchmarks/v3/bench_data_segments_typed_vs_dict.py. Result JSON: benchmarks/v3/results/phase-v3_1-data-segments.json. Bytes-based on both sides (matches the units-only probe's methodology — apples to apples; msgspec.json.Decoder() vs msgspec.json.Decoder(list[T])).

Cassette: same data.json.gz used elsewhere in this report.

Per-segment (typed/dict ratios; <1 = typed is faster/lighter):

Segment Count Speed (×faster) Memory ratio Size ratio units 11,169 4.16× 0.64× 0.66× effect 60,015 1.85× 0.49× 0.49× statMod 288 1.72× 0.56× 0.57× material 858 1.59× 0.59× 0.59× datacronAffixTemplateSet 722 1.51× 0.71× 0.71× skill 1,892 1.50× 0.49× 0.50× equipment 698 1.50× 0.57× 0.58× recipe 2,172 1.48× 0.54× 0.54× datacronTemplate 61 1.43× 0.61× 0.61× statModSet 8 1.25× 0.56× 0.55× ability 6,465 1.12× 0.79× 0.79× datacronSet 10 1.04× 0.75× 0.76× campaign 16 1.04× 1.00× 1.00× datacronHelpEntry 5 1.00× 0.56× 0.53×

Aggregate across all 14 segments:

Metric dict typed ratio Decode wall (sum) ~3,290 ms ~1,840 ms 1.79× faster Peak alloc (sum) ~3.5 GiB ~2.3 GiB 0.66× Resident size (sum) ~3.5 GiB ~2.3 GiB 0.66×

Decision rule (pre-registered in the bench script, identical to the units-only probe): - speed_ratio ≥ 1.5× AND memory_ratio ≤ 0.7× → green-light typing remaining segments. - speed_ratio < 1.2× OR memory_ratio > 0.9× → stop here. - In-between → judgment call.

Outcome: aggregate 1.79× faster AND 0.66× memory — both thresholds met → green-light typing the remaining ~70 /data segments in a follow-up v3.1 phase if operator demand warrants.

Where the typing didn't move the needle: - campaign (1.04× speed, 1.00× memory). 16 entries, but each has a deeply nested campaignMap.campaignNodeDifficultyGroup.campaignNode list that v3.1 leaves as dict[str, Any]. The bulk is in the un-typed sub-tree; typing only the outer envelope barely helps. Deep-typing the campaignNode shape is a future-phase candidate. - ability (1.12× speed). Same story — aiParams, synergy, visualTarget, tier, descriptiveTag left as dicts because their shapes are sparse / inconsistent across the 6,465 entries. - Very small segments (statModSet, datacronSet, datacronHelpEntry). Decode times are sub-millisecond; ratios are noisy and not meaningful.

Caveat: the helper's runtime path uses msgspec.convert on dicts (no JSON re-encode), since callers operate on dicts from GameDataCache or get_game_data. The bench's bytes-based comparison isolates the decoder cost. Real-world cost on the cached path is lower than the bench numbers because msgspec.convert walks the in-memory dict tree directly.

docs.title: v3.1 — typed/dict client split + codegen
docs.text:
Restructures the public surface into two import paths (swgoh_comlink.* = dict-default; swgoh_comlink.typed.* = typed-Struct default) and code-generates all four client classes (sync/async × dict/typed) from a single manifest. See docs/adr/0005-typed-dict-client-split.md and docs/v3/codegen.md.

Metric Before (v3.0) After (v3.1-research) Δ Cold import swgoh_comlink 7.0 ms 7.8 ms +11% (still well under Phase 5's headline) Public client classes 2 4 sync/async × dict/typed Hand-maintained endpoint method bodies 32 (2 clients × 16) 0 (all generated from manifest) full elimination Manifest entries (single source of truth) n/a 15 one entry per uniform endpoint Hand-written escape hatches 8 (per-client) 5 (per surface, in mixins) shared across dict/typed Codegen invariant tests 0 107 guards the 2×2 surface contract

No runtime behavior changes — the four generated clients call the same _post / _request / _retry paths Phase 4 + Phase 2 set up. The codegen lets all four track a single manifest entry per endpoint so a schema change ripples through every variant atomically.

docs.title: v3.1 — async-aware GameDataCache
docs.text:
GameDataCache grows a* twins of every client-touching method (acurrent_version, aget_game_data, aget_localization, aevict_old_versions, aclose) and an async with lifecycle. Blocking diskcache and msgpack ops run on asyncio.to_thread; in-memory hits stay synchronous. Same disk store and memo as the sync surface — a sync warmup script can populate a cache an async runtime reads.

Async cache parity on the same /data cassette:

Path Sync get_game_data Async aget_game_data Notes Cold (fresh disk; full pipeline) 3,462 ms 4,291 ms asyncio.run per-iter loop construction; in a live event loop this overhead is gone. Disk-warm (new instance per call) 3,350 ms (1.0× vs cold) 3,973 ms (1.1× vs async cold) Identical underlying work; +~0.6 ms asyncio.to_thread overhead. In-memory warm (same instance) 0.0003 ms (10⁷×) 0.1034 ms (4.15×10⁴) Bench overstates async warm cost — each iter spins up a fresh event loop. Real per-call cost in a live loop is the same dict access (~0.0003 ms).

The 4.15×10⁴ warm headline still clears the Phase 7 100–1000× target by 40×. Async users were locked out of GameDataCache in v3.0; v3.1 gives them the same disk + memo with the same correctness guarantees.

docs.title: v3.2 — StatCalc internals (bimorphic input + cached game_data)
docs.text:
Runs on v3.2-research (off v3.1-research; v3.0 surface stays frozen per ADR-0001). Three orthogonal axes researched; two winners shipped per the pre-registered decision rule in ADR-0006. The other six candidates stay on throwaway prototype branches.

What shipped

Surface Measured Threshold Verdict A — StatCalc.calc_player_stats(player_struct) bimorphic +22.9 % vs dict input (5.2 ms on a 22.6 ms calc) ≤ 10 % Struct overhead OR ship floor option SHIPS (floor) E — get_statcalc_game_data(client, cache=cache) 25.74 ms → 3.62 ms cold-start (+85.9 %) ≥ 50 % cold-start improvement SHIPS

What didn't

Surface Measured Threshold Verdict B — partial-conversion adapter +21.4 % ≤ 10 % Struct overhead Defer (within ±1 % of A) C — accessor-subclass +23.6 % ≤ 10 % Struct overhead Defer (slightly worse than A) D — ProcessPoolExecutor fan-out 21.59 ms → 25.40 ms at 4w (0.85×) ≥ 2× speedup AND ≤ 1 % serial regression Defer (regresses) F — typed-Struct game_data tables ~+1.3 % (mechanism-bound; micro-bench, no prototype) ≥ 10 % hot-path Defer (mechanism-bound below threshold) G — direct v3.1 typed-segment consumption est. -5 % to +10 % (extrapolation from F's micro-bench; no prototype) ≥ 10 % hot-path Defer (negative-bound payoff) H — hot-table index restructuring +5.7 % targeted variant ≥ 10 % hot-path Defer (aggressive variant broke parity on mod-set bonuses)

Key findings

  • Adapter cost is mechanism-bound by per-Mod conversion. All three bimorphic candidates (A/B/C) land within ±1 % of each other because the bulk of the work is msgspec.to_builtins walking the Mod sub-Structs. B's "skip Player metadata" saves ~0.3 ms; C's "interleave with calc" adds isinstance overhead that cancels the win. Conclusion: the simplest of the three (A) ships; the recipe recommends client.get_player(..., raw=True) for hot loops.
  • Parallelism is the wrong shape for this workload. Python's ProcessPoolExecutor IPC break-even (~500 µs/task even with batching) exceeds StatCalc's per-unit work (~70 µs). Parallel wins on player_small (1.6× at 4w) and loses on player_large (0.85× at 8w) — the result-pickle cost scales with batch size and the serial ship-pass tail eats into the chars-pass gain. Wait for either Cython inner loops (per-unit work grows) or sub-interpreters / free- threaded Python (IPC cost shrinks) before revisiting.
  • Cold-start is the single most leveraged optimization in StatCalc today. Just persisting the normalized form (no algorithmic change) gives 7× faster process startup. Big win for cron jobs and serverless callers; no-op for long-running bots.
  • Plan estimates ran consistently optimistic. Across Phases 2-4, none of the eight candidates exceeded its plan-stated payoff estimate; six fell short or failed entirely. The pre-registered decision rule (written before any measurement) was load-bearing for not shipping things that didn't pay back.

docs.title: v3.3 — StatCalc rewrite research (Phase 1 baseline, ADR-0007)
docs.text:
Runs on v3.3-research (off v3.2-research; v3.0 surface stays frozen per ADR-0001). v3.3 is a broad research sweep — pure-Python restructure + native acceleration (Cython / mypyc / Rust) + algorithmic re-attacks of v3.2's H + a typed-fastpath for the bimorphic +22.9 % cost. Pre-registered decision rule lives in ADR-0007.

Phase 1 baseline (recorded against v3.2 shipped code at SHA ef7a542):

Metric Measured v3.3 ship threshold calc_player_stats(dict) warm, player_large (397 units) 21.8 ms Hot-path: ≤ 19.6 ms (≥ 10 % improvement) calc_player_stats(Player_struct) warm, bimorphic 27.4 ms (+25.8 %) Ergonomics: ≤ 22.9 ms (Struct overhead ≤ 5 %) cold_start: GameDataBuilder + StatCalc.__init__ 24.9 ms already shipped (Candidate E cached path: 3.6 ms) game_data resident size (asizeof, legacy dict tables) 12.9 MB Memory: ≤ 10.3 MB (≥ 20 % reduction) calc_player_stats transient peak, player_large 18.0 MB Informational — no bar msgspec.to_builtins(roster_unit) per-unit cost ~6.0 µs (Phase 4b typed-fastpath target — replace with direct getattr)

Surprises from the Phase 1 measurement (vs. assumptions in the plan):

  • game_data is ~13 MB, not 50–100 MB. Plan over-estimated by ~5×. The ≥ 20 % reduction bar (≤ 10.3 MB target) is still meaningful but a smaller absolute win than imagined. Worth keeping as a metric; not worth blocking a ship on it alone.
  • _format_stats is the new #1 cProfile consumer, not _table_get. Cumulative time: _format_stats 119 ms (39 %) vs _table_get 85 ms (28 %). The v3.2 cProfile attribution noted _table_get because it was the loudest individual function; once you sum the inner work _format_stats does, it dominates. Phase 2's decomposition target is well-placed.
  • Bimorphic conversion confirmed as 100 % to_builtins. cProfile dump shows _to_dict_if_struct + msgspec._core.to_builtins together = 22 ms of the 330 ms profile run, exactly matching the bench's +25.8 % overhead. Phase 4b's typed-fastpath has a surgically clear target.

Subsequent Phase 2–4 prototype branches measure against this baseline. Phase 5 will fill in the per-candidate matrix here once the integration commit lands.

Phase 5 outcome (recorded against v3.3 integration HEAD):

Surface Measured Threshold Verdict calc_player_stats(dict) warm, v3.3 integration 18.24 ms (+16.3 % vs v3.2 baseline 21.80 ms) ≥ 10 % hot-path SHIPS calc_player_stats(Player_struct) via typed-fastpath +10.1 % overhead (down from v3.2 +22.9 %) ≤ 5 % bimorphic Below bar; ships as partial-win game_data resident size unchanged at 12.9 MB ≥ 20 % Nothing shipped (no candidate targeted memory)

Candidate matrix (all measured on player_large warm; v3.2 dict baseline = 21.80 ms):

Candidate Branch Hot-path Ergonomics Verdict Phase 2 — pure-Python restructure pure-python-restructure +8.7 % — Ships combined Phase 3a — Cython + Phase 2 cython-prototype +17.8 % — Cleared but distribution cost too high — defer Phase 3b — mypyc + Phase 2 mypyc-prototype +15.0 % — Cleared but distribution cost too high — defer Phase 3c — Rust/PyO3 + Phase 2 rust-kernel-prototype est. ~+10-15 % — Mechanism-bound below Cython — defer Phase 4a — Candidate H re-attack not prototyped est. ~+5-8 % alone — Defer (covered by Cython in combined results) Phase 4b — typed-fastpath typed-fastpath — +10.1 % bimorphic overhead Ships as partial-win Phase 2 + 4b integration final-integration +16.3 % bimorphic +10.1 % (down from +22.9 %) SHIPS

Key v3.3 finding: the 15-wheel-per-release native distribution matrix is the binding constraint on Cython/mypyc/Rust shipping, not their raw speed. All three cleared (or near-cleared) the 10 % hot-path bar, but for a research library serving a small SWGOH community the +6-9 percentage points of additional speed do not justify 30-60 min of CI per release tag. Pure-Python restructure + typed-fastpath together cleared the bar without the distribution complexity. Native variants stay on throwaway prototype branches as future options.

docs.title: What v3 didn't deliver (deferred to v3.1/v3.2)
docs.text:
• [ratelimit] + [circuitbreaker] extras — ADR-0004
  • ~~Async-aware StatCalc with threshold-based ProcessPoolExecutor~~ — prototyped in v3.2; D regresses on large rosters; deferred without ship (ADR-0006)
  • StatCalc/ → statcalc/ PEP 8 rename
  • Deeper Mod.equipment / unit_stat typing (needs non-empty cassette samples)
  • ~~Async-aware GameDataCache for SwgohComlinkAsync~~ — landed in v3.1-research
  • ~~GameDataBuilder rewrite atop GameDataCache~~ — landed in v3.2-research as get_statcalc_game_data helper (ADR-0006)
  • unasync-style codegen to actually eliminate sync/async duplication
  • stamina dependency — never added (Phase 2 hand-rolled the retry loop)
  • globals.py rename — collides with the builtin globals() function inside __init__.py; works today but is a known foot-gun

docs.title: What v3 delivered beyond plan
docs.text:
• compat.to_pydantic(struct, model_class) — dynamic adapter without doubling the type surface. The plan called for as_model=True per endpoint method; the helper form serves the same need with zero kwarg explosion.
  • GameDataCache in-memory memo — the plan only specified disk caching. The realistic 10⁷× win comes from same-instance dict lookups; disk alone gives ~1×.

docs.title: How to reproduce
docs.text:
# Fresh checkout + native ARM Python 3.11
git clone <repo>
cd comlink-python-v3
uv venv --python 3.11
uv sync --group dev

# Record cassettes (once, with a live comlink + ally codes)
COMLINK_URL=http://your.comlink.local:3000 \
SMALL_ROSTER_ALLYCODE=<small> \
LARGE_ROSTER_ALLYCODE=<large> \
GUILD_ID=<guild-id> \
uv run python -m benchmarks.v3._record

# Run every bench from this report
uv run python -m benchmarks.v3.bench_v3_final

Per-phase per-bench results land in benchmarks/v3/results/phase-*.json.

docs.title: Caveats
docs.text:
• All numbers are on one machine. Phase-to-phase comparisons are valid (same hardware, same Python, same cassettes); cross-platform / cross-CPU comparisons aren't.
  • Timing benches drift 30–50% run-to-run on a working laptop. Memory baselines (deterministic — same bytes in, same allocations out) are the stable signal. Documented per-phase as an open question.
  • The Phase 3 plan's "Mann-Whitney U at p<0.05 on every comparative claim" was downgraded to "MWU only on Phase 3 headlines" (Plan D10). This report relies on consistent direction-of-change across multiple runs rather than statistical hypothesis testing per metric.

docs.title: Code generation for the client matrix
docs.text:
swgoh_comlink ships four client classes — sync and async, each in dict-default and typed-Struct flavours:

Import Default return Use for from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink dict[str, Any] v2 wire compat from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlinkAsync dict[str, Any] v2 wire compat (async) from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink msgspec.Struct Typed attribute access from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlinkAsync msgspec.Struct Typed attribute access (async)

All four classes are generated from a single manifest. This page is the contributor guide for working with the generator.

docs.title: Folder layout
docs.text:
src/swgoh_comlink/
├── _codegen/
│   ├── endpoints.py            ← single source of truth (manifest)
│   ├── templates/
│   │   └── client.py.jinja     ← one template, parameterised on is_async + is_typed
│   ├── generate.py             ← writes the 4 files below + runs ruff
│   └── README.md
├── _escape_hatches_sync.py     ← hand-written mixin: healthcheck, raw_request, stream_*
├── _escape_hatches_async.py    ← async twin
├── swgoh_comlink.py            ← GENERATED dict-default sync
├── swgoh_comlink_async.py      ← GENERATED dict-default async
└── typed/
    ├── __init__.py             ← hand-written: re-exports
    ├── swgoh_comlink.py        ← GENERATED typed sync
    └── swgoh_comlink_async.py  ← GENERATED typed async

Generated files start with # AUTOGENERATED — DO NOT EDIT. and a pre-commit hook (codegen-drift) refuses commits where they diverge from the manifest.

docs.title: Regenerating
docs.text:
make generate
# equivalent:
uv run python -m swgoh_comlink._codegen.generate

The generator writes the four output files, then runs ruff check --fix (which includes import sorting) and ruff format. Generator whitespace doesn't matter — ruff is the source of truth for the final file shape.

docs.title: Adding an endpoint
docs.text:
1. Open src/swgoh_comlink/_codegen/endpoints.py and append one Endpoint(...) entry to ENDPOINTS.

  2. For a uniform endpoint (payload from a builder, no special logic), the entry looks like:

Endpoint(
    name="get_my_thing",
    http_method="POST",
    path="myThing",
    docstring="One-line method docstring.",
    params=(
        Param("foo", "str"),
        Param("bar", "int", default="0"),
    ),
    payload_builder="my_thing_payload",
    aliases=("getMyThing",),
)
  1. For a typed endpoint (returns a Struct, accepts raw=), add:
    typed_decoder="MY_THING_DECODER",
    typed_return="MyThing",

Or for envelope-unwrap semantics like /guild:

    typed_decoder_callable="decode_my_thing",
    typed_return="MyThing",
    dict_decoder_callable="decode_my_thing_dict",

  1. For quirks (pre-fetch metadata fallback, stats sub-service, custom timeout, @param_alias decorator, inline payload), the relevant flags are documented in the Endpoint dataclass fields.

  2. Regenerate and verify:

make generate
make generate-check   # confirms idempotent
uv run pytest tests/v3/test_codegen_invariants.py -q
  1. Commit the manifest change + the four regenerated files in the same commit. The pre-commit hook will block a manifest change without its corresponding regenerated output.

docs.title: When to bypass the manifest
docs.text:
Methods with non-uniform shape stay hand-written in mixins:

  • healthcheck — bool return, exception-safe, bypasses retry.
  • raw_request — httpx.Response return.
  • stream_game_data / stream_localization — streaming context managers, bypass retry.
  • get_latest_game_data_version — wraps get_game_metadata.

These live in _escape_hatches_sync.py / _escape_hatches_async.py. The generated client classes inherit from the appropriate mixin.

If a new endpoint genuinely doesn't fit the manifest shape, add it to the mixin — don't bend the manifest schema to accommodate one outlier.

docs.title: Reading the generated files
docs.text:
Generated files have:

  • A # AUTOGENERATED — DO NOT EDIT. banner pointing to the source.
  • Imports + module docstring tailored to the (sync/async, dict/typed) variant.
  • class SwgohComlink(SwgohComlinkBase, _SyncEscapeHatchMixin): (or its 3 cousins).
  • __init__, lifecycle (__enter__/__exit__ or __aenter__/__aexit__), _request / _post / _get_game_version.
  • One method per Endpoint in the manifest, followed by alias assignments (getMyThing = get_my_thing).

If something in the generated output looks wrong, edit the manifest (for endpoint shape) or the template (for boilerplate). Never edit a generated file directly — your edit will be overwritten on the next make generate.

docs.title: The codegen invariant tests
docs.text:
tests/v3/test_codegen_invariants.py exercises the generator's output without exercising the wire:

  • Every manifest endpoint exists on all four client classes.
  • Every alias resolves to the canonical method.
  • Sync and async signatures match within a surface (modulo async).
  • Dict and typed signatures have the same parameter names; only raw's default differs (False on typed, True on dict for source-compat).

Plus two end-to-end parity tests: dict client returns dict for get_player; typed client returns Player Struct.

A failure in these tests means the generator drifted from its contract — check the template + manifest before touching anything else.

docs.text:

  • src/swgoh_comlink/_codegen/README.md — quick reference at the generator's own folder.

docs.title: Installing the v3 alpha safely
docs.text:
The v3 alpha ships as the same package name (swgoh_comlink) as the stable v2.x release on PyPI, but it is not on PyPI — it is only available as a GitHub Release asset on MarTrepodi/comlink-python (see ADR-0008). That name-sharing is deliberate (the alpha is the future of the same package), but it means you should install it in a way that can't silently interfere with — or be silently replaced by — the public v2.x release. This guide covers exactly that.

Rule zero: never install the alpha into a shared or system environment. Always use a dedicated virtual environment.

docs.title: 1. Isolated install (recommended)
docs.text:
Create a virtual environment used only for the alpha:

# with uv (recommended)
uv venv .venv-swgoh-v3
source .venv-swgoh-v3/bin/activate    # Windows: .venv-swgoh-v3\Scripts\activate
uv pip install https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a2/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a2-py3-none-any.whl

# stdlib equivalent
python3.11 -m venv .venv-swgoh-v3
source .venv-swgoh-v3/bin/activate
pip install https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a2/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a2-py3-none-any.whl

Verify what you got:

python -c "import swgoh_comlink; print(swgoh_comlink.version)"
# -> 3.0.0a2

Your existing v2 environments are untouched — the alpha lives only inside .venv-swgoh-v3, and deleting that directory removes it completely.

docs.title: 2. Guard against silent replacement by PyPI v2.x
docs.text:
Because the alpha is not on PyPI, any later dependency resolution that re-installs swgoh_comlink from PyPI can only find v2.x. Pin the alpha in a constraints file so that scenario fails loudly instead of silently downgrading you:

# constraints.txt
swgoh_comlink==3.0.0a2

pip install -c constraints.txt <anything-else-you-add-to-this-env>

With the pin in place, a resolver that tries to fetch swgoh_comlink from PyPI errors out ("no matching distribution for swgoh_comlink==3.0.0a2") rather than replacing your alpha with v2.x.

Notes on specific commands:

  • pip install -U swgoh_comlink will not downgrade you — pip sees the installed 3.0.0a2 as newer than anything on PyPI and keeps it.
  • pip install --force-reinstall swgoh_comlink (or uninstall + reinstall by name) will land you on v2.x, because by-name installs resolve against PyPI. Reinstall from the wheel URL instead.

docs.title: 3. uv-managed projects
docs.text:
If the consuming project is uv-managed, pin the alpha as a direct-URL source so the lockfile records exactly this artifact:

uv add "swgoh_comlink @ https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a2/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a2-py3-none-any.whl"

uv.lock then holds the URL + hash; uv sync reproduces the alpha exactly and will never "helpfully" resolve swgoh_comlink from PyPI.

docs.title: 4. Switching back to the public v2.x release
docs.text:
Preferred: throw away the alpha environment. Nothing to undo:

deactivate
rm -rf .venv-swgoh-v3

Your v2 environments were never touched.

In-place rollback (same environment), if you must:

pip uninstall -y swgoh_comlink
pip install "swgoh_comlink==2.*"

(Remove the constraints.txt pin first, and the direct-URL source / uv.lock entry in uv-managed projects.)

Rolling back the package does not roll back your code

Code written against the v3 typed surface (from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink, msgspec.Struct returns, GameDataCache, bimorphic StatCalc) will not run on v2.x. If you adopted v3 APIs, switching back means reverting those call sites too — the migration guide documents the v2 ↔ v3 differences. Code that only ever used the dict-default from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink works identically on both.

docs.title: Reporting problems
docs.text: Open issues at MarTrepodi/comlink-python/issues with the v3 label — see the release notes for what to include.

docs.title: v2 → v3 Migration Guide
docs.text:
v3 is a major version with one breaking change (Python floor bumped to 3.11) and a handful of non-breaking additions. v2 dict semantics are preserved on the default import path — from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink returns dicts exactly like v2. Opt into the typed msgspec.Struct surface by switching to from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink.

On the typed surface, raw=True returns the v2 dict for a single call (see Soft migration). The dict-default surface accepts the same keyword and ignores it, so library code stays portable across both surfaces.

For automated detection of patterns that need updating, run::

swgoh-migrate path/to/your/code

The migration tool flags v2 patterns as ERROR / WARNING / INFO. v2→v3 rule ids start with V3* (vs DEP* for the v1→v2 rules).

docs.title: Quick reference
docs.text: Concern v2 v3 Python version ≥3.10 ≥3.11 (ADR-0002) import swgoh_comlink cold time ~65 ms ~7 ms (lazy via PEP 562) get_player(...) from swgoh_comlink dict dict (unchanged) get_player(...) from swgoh_comlink.typed n/a Player (msgspec.Struct) Same pattern for get_guild, get_game_metadata, get_leaderboard dict dict OR typed Struct per import path Other endpoints (get_game_data, get_localization, get_enums, …) dict dict (both import paths) Retry on transient errors none (v2.3+: opt-in retry=RetryPolicy(...)) opt-in retry=RetryPolicy(...); default is one attempt HTTP errors SwgohComlinkException (v2.3+: typed SwgohComlinkHTTPError subclasses) typed SwgohComlinkHTTPError subclasses HMAC auth unchanged unchanged Connection pool httpx defaults profile="default" preset HTTP client injection n/a http_client= kwarg Cache for /data + /localization n/a GameDataCache ([cache] extra) Pydantic adapter n/a compat.to_pydantic(struct, BaseModel) ([pydantic] extra) Sync/async parity identical signatures identical signatures

docs.title: Two import paths: dict-default vs typed
docs.text:
v3 ships two parallel client surfaces. Pick by import path; the underlying transport, retry, and caching are shared.

# Dict-default surface (matches v2 wire shape exactly)
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, SwgohComlinkAsync

with SwgohComlink(url="...") as client:
    player = client.get_player(allycode=123456789)
    name = player["name"]              # dict indexing — v2 style
    guild_id = player["guildId"]
    roster = player["rosterUnit"]

# Typed surface (msgspec.Struct attribute access)
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink, SwgohComlinkAsync

with SwgohComlink(url="...") as client:
    player = client.get_player(allycode=123456789)
    name = player.name                 # attribute access — typed
    guild_id = player.guild_id         # snake_case Python; camelCase on the wire
    roster = player.roster_unit
    first_def = player.roster_unit[0].definition_id

The typed surface uses msgspec's rename="camel" so wire camelCase maps to PEP-8 snake_case fields automatically.

docs.title: Why two surfaces
docs.text:
ADR-0005 records the rationale. Short version:

  • v2 wire compat preserved on the default import — no behavior change for existing v2 callers.
  • Typed access opt-in via a one-line import change.
  • Both surfaces share transport, retry, decoding, caching code; only the response shape differs.
  • All four client classes (sync/async × dict/typed) are code-generated from a single manifest (src/swgoh_comlink/_codegen/endpoints.py) via Jinja + ruff. See docs/v3/codegen.md.

docs.title: Soft migration: raw=True
docs.text:
If you can't (or don't want to) migrate dict-indexing code yet, every typed endpoint accepts raw=True to return the v2 dict shape unchanged:

# v3 with raw=True — v2 semantics preserved
player = client.get_player(allycode=123456789, raw=True)
name = player["name"]  # works exactly like v2

Same for get_guild, get_game_metadata, get_leaderboard. The dict shape is byte-identical with v2 (we test this via the Phase 1 golden suite).

docs.title: Soft migration: compat.to_dict()
docs.text:
For one-shot conversions where you have a Struct but need a dict:

from swgoh_comlink import compat

p = client.get_player(allycode=123456789)
as_dict = compat.to_dict(p)  # warns DeprecationWarning
name = as_dict["name"]

compat.to_dict() is marked for removal in v3.2. Prefer attribute access or raw=True.

docs.title: New client kwargs
docs.text:
# v2
client = SwgohComlink(url="http://localhost:3000")

# v3 — new optional kwargs
from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy

client = SwgohComlink(
    url="http://localhost:3000",
    http_client=my_httpx_client,   # inject your own; SDK won't close it
    profile="bot",                  # connection pool preset
    retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=3),  # opt-in; default None = one attempt
)
  • http_client= lets you inject your own httpx.Client/httpx.AsyncClient. When supplied, the SDK does NOT auto-close it.
  • profile="default" | "bot" | "bulk" selects a connection-pool preset (keepalive 30s / 120s / 60s; pool sizes tuned for each use case).
  • retry=RetryPolicy(...) opts in to retrying rate refusals and HTTP 503 (see Retry semantics). The default, retry=None, makes exactly one attempt per call, as in v2.

docs.title: Retry semantics
docs.text:
Retries are opt-in and use the same RetryPolicy as the v2.3+ line. By default (retry=None) a call makes exactly one attempt, with no waiting, and raises a typed HTTP error on failure. Pass a RetryPolicy to retry the failures that mean the call was not carried out: rate refusals (SwgohComlinkRateLimitError: HTTP 429 or the game's Rate exceeded!) and HTTP 503 (SwgohComlinkUnavailableError). Retry-After is honoured (capped at max_retry_after), otherwise the client waits for the next backoff value plus jitter. Other errors, including connection drops and other 4xx/5xx statuses, are raised at once. A policy can also pace calls per endpoint (min_interval), and a rate refusal holds back the endpoint it came from so concurrent callers back off together.

from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy

# v2 / v3 default — one attempt, then raise
try:
    player = client.get_player(allycode=...)
except SwgohComlinkRateLimitError:
    ...

# v3 with retries on rate refusals and 503
client = SwgohComlink(url=..., retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=3, min_interval=0.4))

Alpha note. 3.0.0a1 retried 408/425/429/5xx three times by default via a max_retries= keyword. That keyword and the default retrying were removed in 3.0.0a2 in favour of the opt-in retry= policy above.

docs.title: with_options(...) for one-off tweaks
docs.text:
# v3 — shallow clone with overrides; underlying httpx client is SHARED
patient = client.with_options(retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=5))
patient.get_player(allycode=...)  # retried per the new policy
no_retry = client.with_options(retry=None)
no_retry.get_player(allycode=...)  # one attempt, then raise

docs.title: Reading game metadata
docs.text:
get_game_metadata() keeps the v2 dict on the default import, and the SDK's own version lookups (_get_game_version, get_latest_game_data_version) request the dict form on both surfaces, so code that shadows them needs no change. Only the typed client returns a Metadata Struct:

# Default import: unchanged from v2
md = client.get_game_metadata()
version = md["latestGamedataVersion"]

# Typed surface (from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink)
md = client.get_game_metadata()
version = md.latest_gamedata_version

docs.title: New: ergonomics methods
docs.text:
# v3: bot startup probe
if not client.healthcheck(timeout=5.0):
    raise SystemExit("comlink unreachable")

# v3: escape hatch for endpoints the SDK doesn't model
response = client.raw_request("POST", "/custom/path", payload={...})

# v3: stream large /data without materializing in memory
with client.stream_game_data(version="...") as r:
    r.raise_for_status()
    for chunk in r.iter_bytes():
        process(chunk)

docs.title: New: GameDataCache for repeated /data / /localization
docs.text:
# v3 with [cache] extra
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink._cache import GameDataCache

client = SwgohComlink(url="...")
cache = GameDataCache()  # XDG-compliant default cache dir

# First call: full fetch + decode + msgpack encode + disk write (~3.5s for /data)
data = cache.get_game_data(client)

# Subsequent calls on the same cache instance: in-memory dict hit (~0.0003ms)
data = cache.get_game_data(client)

The cache is version-aware. When comlink's game version bumps, the metadata probe (memoized in a 30s TTLCache) notices, fetches fresh data, and tags it with the new version. Call cache.evict_old_versions(...) to clean up stale entries.

docs.title: New: Pydantic adapter
docs.text:
# v3 with [pydantic] extra
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from swgoh_comlink import compat

class MyPlayer(BaseModel):
    name: str
    ally_code: str = Field(alias="allyCode")
    level: int
    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}

player = client.get_player(allycode=...)
my_player = compat.to_pydantic(player, MyPlayer)  # full pydantic validation

The bridge goes Struct → dict (via msgspec.to_builtins) → BaseModel (via model_validate). User-defined BaseModel keeps the type surface on YOUR side — the SDK doesn't ship parallel pydantic types per endpoint.

docs.title: Helper functions (helpers/)
docs.text:
get_guild_members, async_get_guild_members, and the GAC helpers (get_gac_brackets, async_get_gac_brackets, get_current_gac_event) still exist with their v2 signatures. They internally pass raw=True to the typed endpoints so their dict-shape contract is preserved.

If you call them directly, no migration needed. If you call them and then index into the result (get_guild_members(...)[0]["playerId"]), that still works.

docs.title: Imports
docs.text:
# v2
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, SwgohComlinkAsync, StatCalc, GameDataBuilder

# v3 — same imports work, but they're now LAZY (PEP 562 __getattr__)
# First access triggers the import + caches; subsequent accesses are O(1).
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, SwgohComlinkAsync, StatCalc, GameDataBuilder

import swgoh_comlink no longer pulls in httpx, msgspec, or the StatCalc subpackage. They load on first use of the public name they gate.

docs.title: What was removed / deprecated
docs.text: Removed Replacement Python 3.10 support Bump to 3.11+ max_retries= keyword and _retry.py (alpha 1 only; never in v2) retry=RetryPolicy(...), opt-in (none) (no public API was actually removed in v3.0) Deprecated Removed in swgoh_comlink.compat.to_dict() v3.2

docs.title: Not in v3.0 (deferred to v3.1)
docs.text:
• [ratelimit] extra with aiometer / aiolimiter integration (ADR-0004). For now, use vanilla asyncio.Semaphore — see docs/v3/recipes/operator-side-concurrency.md.
  • [circuitbreaker] extra with purgatory integration (ADR-0004).
  • Async-aware StatCalc (calc_roster_stats_async with threshold-based ProcessPoolExecutor).
  • Deeper Mod.primary_stat / equipment typing (Phase 3.5 hit the level of typing that produces real wins; deeper still moves the needle slowly).
  • StatCalc/ → statcalc/ directory rename (PEP 8 cleanup; deferred for the import-site churn).

docs.title: Want the v2 behavior in v3?
docs.text:
You already have it: from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink returns dicts exactly like v2, so dict-indexing code needs no change.

If you have moved to the typed surface and need the dict for one call, pass raw=True:

from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink

client = SwgohComlink(url="...")
player = client.get_player(allycode=..., raw=True)
# `player` is a dict; index it like v2.

docs.text: swgoh-migrate path/to/your/code flags every v2 pattern with a human-readable suggestion. Run it pre-flight before you cut over.

docs.text: Plan said Reality Why benchmarks/v3/_harness.py provides measure / track_memory / track_import_time / Reporter Same surface; also added load_cassette, cassette_exists, require_python_version, MeasureResult, MemoryResult dataclasses, and git_sha() helper Smaller call sites; pinning Python version makes phase-to-phase comparison defensible (cross-cutting principle in plan). bench_baseline.py runs every metric Cassette-bound metrics emit status="skip" when their cassette is missing Lets the harness be runnable on a fresh clone before the operator has recorded cassettes, which preserves the "everything is reproducible from this commit" property. Plan refers to get_data and get_metadata endpoints The v2 source actually exposes get_game_data and get_game_metadata Used the actual method names in the harness; cassette names stay as data / metadata for plan continuity. Plan calls out wheel/site-packages size in baseline Moved behind --full flag The metric requires a network-free uv build plus venv-install dance; expensive on every run and not needed until Phase 6 extras work compares against it. "Small" roster cassette ~50 units player_small uses ally code 855566316 (115 units). Closer to small than large but not literally 50. Smallest representative roster available on this comlink. Distinct enough from player_large (397 units) to expose decode/scale differences. Exit criterion "cassettes sum to under 5 MB" Reality is ~18 MB on disk (/data alone is 15 MB gzipped) The full /data payload is load-bearing for Phase 3's headline numbers; can't shrink it without invalidating the comparison. Plan exit criterion updated to ~15–20 MB. Python interpreter Required a rebuild against aarch64 cpython-3.11.15 (uv-managed). Initial venv landed on /usr/local/opt/python@3.11 which is x86_64 under Rosetta. (a) Rosetta perf would skew benchmarks; (b) x86 Homebrew Python lacks macOS Local Network privacy grant and silently fails LAN connections with EHOSTUNREACH.

docs.title: Open questions
docs.text:
• The Local Network privacy grant is per-binary on macOS. Any future bench/test runner that talks to LAN comlink will need the same grant once. Document this in CONTRIBUTING / quickstart when those exist.
  • Cassette regeneration policy is documented (fixtures/README.md), but there's no automated drift detector. If upstream comlink changes a field, the cassette goes stale silently. Consider adding a "shape signature" (sorted set of top-level keys per endpoint) to the result JSON so drift is visible across phases.
  • Should bench_install_size also measure site-packages delta (not just wheel size)? Currently only the wheel size is reported. A site-packages measurement requires creating a fresh venv and installing — defer until Phase 6 needs it.

docs.title: Benchmark deltas vs baseline
docs.text:
Phase 0 is the baseline. Numbers from benchmarks/v3/results/phase-0-baseline.json on Python 3.11.15 (aarch64, native) at SHA 470debd.

Metric Median p95 Unit Phase target cold_import_time 65.4 — ms Phase 5: ≤6 ms (10× reduction). httpx_loaded_on_import 1.0 (yes) — bool Phase 5: 0. method_body_duplication_ratio 1.0 (16/16 methods) — ratio Phase 4: <0.10. get_player_small_e2e_latency (115 units) 0.29 0.56 ms Phase 2 + 3: ≤0.15 ms target. get_player_large_e2e_latency (397 units) 40.1 121.4 ms Phase 3 headline (Struct decode). get_data_decode_time (json) 7,120.2 7,924 ms Phase 3 headline: 3–5× faster (≤2 s). get_data_decode_peak_memory 1,392.4 MiB — bytes Phase 3 headline: 4–6× lower (≤350 MiB). get_data_object_size 1,033.7 MiB — bytes Phase 3 headline: 40–60% smaller (≤500 MiB). get_player_concurrent_100x_async_wall (small cassette) 81.4 89.5 ms Phase 2 / 3 stress baseline. get_player_concurrent_100x_async_peak_memory 24.9 MiB — bytes Phase 2 / 3 baseline. installed_wheel_size (--full) — — bytes Deferred to Phase 6.

The cold_import_time figure drifted from 41.1 ms (first run) to 65.4 ms here on the same machine + interpreter — system load during the run. Phase 5's target is "≤6 ms"; any value in that range is unambiguously a 10× win regardless of which baseline value we anchor against. The plan's "±5% reproducibility" exit-criterion is unrealistic for cold-import on a working machine; document as an open question.

docs.title: Notable cassette-free finding
docs.text: method_body_duplication_ratio = 1.0 (perfect duplication) across all 16 paired get_* methods. Higher than the plan's predicted ~0.65. Sync and async bodies are literally identical after stripping await and async — the codemod for Phase 4 will be near-mechanical rather than per-method.

docs.title: Notable cassette-bound findings
docs.text:
/data decode at baseline is enormous. A single get_game_data() call decodes ~15 MB of gzipped JSON into a Python dict graph that:

  • takes 7.5 seconds to parse with stdlib json,
  • peaks at 1.39 GiB of allocations during decoding,
  • settles at 1.03 GiB resident.

This is the headline Phase 3 target. Even hitting just the low end of the projected msgspec wins (3× faster, 4× less memory) would drop this to ~2.5 s and ~350 MiB — qualitatively different for any bot operator running on a small VPS. Hitting the projected ceiling (~5× faster, ~6× less) is transformative.

/player end-to-end latency is dominated by JSON decode at 397 units. The 25–28 ms median is mostly the cost of json.loads(358 KiB) plus dict allocation, not the (negligible) mock-transport overhead. Phase 3's typed decode + Phase 5's lazy imports both move this number.

100× async concurrent wall time is 81 ms through the small cassette (115 units, 7.5 KiB gzipped) with peak 25 MiB. ~0.8 ms per call wall-clock. Mostly mock-transport + asyncio scheduling overhead at this size; Phase 5 (lazy imports — avoid pulling httpx during client construction) and Phase 3 (faster decode) are the levers, but the absolute numbers are already small. This benchmark exists to catch regressions in async overhead, not to be the headline.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text: Plan said Reality Why Add stamina>=24.3 to [project.dependencies] and use it for retries No stamina dependency. Hand-rolled retry loop in _retry.py (~50 lines stdlib). Stamina v24 has no way to let an attempt's exception influence the upcoming sleep duration -- which is exactly what Retry-After support requires. A hand-rolled loop honors Retry-After and falls back to compute_backoff cleanly, with zero deps. Create new module src/swgoh_comlink/_base_client.py housing _BaseClient Extended existing SwgohComlinkBase in src/swgoh_comlink/_base.py _base.py already exists and serves the same role. Adding a parallel _base_client.py would have created multiple-inheritance ambiguity. Both clients inherit from the extended SwgohComlinkBase; the surface is identical to what the plan asked for. 1000 successful requests through the mock for bench_retry_overhead 50 iters x 10 warmup A successful happy-path call is ~150 us; 50 iters smooths jitter; running 1000 buys nothing extra. The reported median is statistically tight. Skip bench_pool_warm.py (not strictly required for exit) Skipped Would require either a real-network round trip or contrived asyncio.sleep-based timing, neither of which is informative; Phase 5 / Phase 7 pool-warm tests will be more meaningful with real workloads.

docs.title: Benchmark deltas vs Phase 0 baseline
docs.text:
Re-ran bench_baseline.py against the Phase 2 working tree (results/phase-2-baseline.json):

Metric Phase 0 Phase 2 Delta Reading cold_import_time 65.4 ms 32.8 ms -49.8 % system noise (see open question) get_player_small_e2e_latency 0.29 ms 0.26 ms -11 % noise get_player_large_e2e_latency 40.1 ms 17.4 ms -56 % noise get_data_decode_time 7,120 ms 3,037 ms -57 % noise get_data_decode_peak_memory 1392.4 MiB 1392.4 MiB 0.0 % algorithmic identity get_data_object_size 1033.7 MiB 1033.7 MiB 0.0 % algorithmic identity get_player_concurrent_100x_async_wall 81 ms 42 ms -49 % noise get_player_concurrent_100x_async_peak_memory 24.9 MiB 24.9 MiB 0.0 % algorithmic identity method_body_duplication_ratio 1.0 1.0 -- unchanged (Phase 4's target, not Phase 2's)

Reading: the memory baselines (which are deterministic -- same cassette bytes -> same allocations -> same object graph) are byte-identical across Phase 0 and Phase 2. That's strong evidence of zero algorithmic regression. The timing "improvements" of 50-57% are run-to-run system noise on the same machine, in the opposite direction of any plausible retry-wrapping overhead. The bench_retry_overhead microbenchmark (quieter, more iters) reports -1.10 % overhead -- within noise. Both agree on the substantive question: Phase 2 introduces no measurable overhead.

The plan's literal exit criterion "Phase 0 baselines unchanged within +/-5%" is unrealistic for cold-import + e2e-latency measurements on a working laptop (already flagged in the Phase 1 report). The spirit -- "no regression" -- is met.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text: Plan said Reality Why Define Structs for every endpoint return type (Metadata, Enums, Events, NameSpaces, SegmentedContent, Player, Unit, Skill, Mod, GuildProfile, LeaderboardEntry, GameDataSegment, Localization) Typed only Player, Metadata, Guild, Leaderboard + their nested types (RosterUnit, Mod, Skill, Relic, ModStat, Member, GuildProfile, LeaderboardEnvelope). Enums/Events/NameSpaces/SegmentedContent stay as untyped dict (passthrough). GameDataSegment stays untyped. Localization stays untyped. 82 segments in /data x ~50 fields each is days of work for a research-phase milestone. Typing the high-traffic endpoints delivers the architecture + most of the visible wins. Deeper typing for /data segments is a Phase 7 (GameDataCache) candidate. Mann-Whitney U at p<0.05 on every Phase 3 comparative claim Not applied. Reports raw medians + ratios. scipy is a heavy dependency for one bench file; the deltas we observe (1.5-2.5x speed, 1.25x memory) are far above scheduler noise (~5-10 %) and don't need a stat test to be defensible. If/when the headline numbers become a public marketing claim, add scipy and the MWU then. raw=True keyword on every endpoint method Added only to the 4 typed endpoints. Other endpoints (already passthrough) didn't need the keyword. A passthrough endpoint already returns dict; raw=True on it would be a no-op. The user contract for non-typed endpoints is unchanged. Update all Phase 1 golden tests to assert attribute access produces the same data Golden tests round-trip via msgspec.to_builtins then dict-compare. Shape tests use attribute access. Net effect is identical (both forms of access work). Round-trip-through-dict is the lossless-round-trip assertion the plan also demanded of compat.to_dict() — one assertion form covers both needs. v2 helpers and get_latest_game_data_version migrated to attribute access _get_game_version and get_latest_game_data_version use attribute access. helpers/_guild.py and helpers/_gac.py call typed endpoints with raw=True. Migrating every helper to attribute access is in-scope for v3.1 / v3.2; for Phase 3 we make the helpers v2-shape-compatible to keep v2 unit tests green without churning the helper internals.

docs.title: Decode speed (bench_decode_speed.py)
docs.text:
Median decode time per cassette × parser. Speed ratio vs stdlib json.

Cassette json msgspec untyped msgspec typed metadata (40 KiB) 0.08 ms (1.0x) 0.05 ms (1.77x) 0.05 ms (1.74x) guild (27 KiB) 0.07 ms (1.0x) 0.04 ms (1.98x) 0.04 ms (1.66x) leaderboard (29 KiB) 0.09 ms (1.0x) 0.04 ms (2.01x) 0.04 ms (2.04x) player_small (58 KiB) 0.18 ms (1.0x) 0.10 ms (1.78x) 0.08 ms (2.45x) player_large (3.6 MiB) 15.4 ms (1.0x) 10.6 ms (1.46x) 9.8 ms (1.57x) data (384 MiB JSON) 3,135 ms (1.0x) 3,144 ms (1.00x) n/a localization (15 MiB) 14.9 ms (1.0x) 8.75 ms (1.70x) n/a

Findings:

  • Where Structs are deep, the typed win materializes (player_small: 2.45x).
  • /data shows no improvement at all — both stdlib json and msgspec untyped land at ~3.1 s for the 384 MiB decoded blob. This is the partial-typing tradeoff stated up front. The "3-5x faster on /data" projection in the original plan required deep segment typing that this phase deliberately deferred.
  • Untyped msgspec beats stdlib json everywhere except /data, where they tie. The crossover suggests msgspec's per-character overhead is comparable on shapes that contain mostly large dicts; the win is in shape-aware code paths.

docs.title: Decode memory (bench_decode_memory.py)
docs.text:
Peak tracemalloc allocation. Ratio = json / parser (higher = better for parser).

Cassette json msgspec untyped msgspec typed metadata 0.22 MiB 0.19 MiB (1.21x) 0.18 MiB (1.21x) guild 0.10 MiB 0.10 MiB (0.99x) 0.08 MiB (1.23x) leaderboard 0.14 MiB 0.11 MiB (1.27x) 0.11 MiB (1.29x) player_small 0.31 MiB 0.26 MiB (1.17x) 0.14 MiB (2.26x) player_large 17.7 MiB 14.9 MiB (1.19x) 13.8 MiB (1.28x) data 1,392 MiB 1,115 MiB (1.25x) n/a

Findings:

  • player_small shows a 2.26x peak-memory reduction — the cleanest typed win in the suite.
  • player_large only nets 1.28x because the large player's dominant memory is in the ~6 mods × 397 units = 2,400 Mod objects, whose internal stats (primary_stat, level_cost, etc.) are still dict[str, Any] and don't get the slotted savings.
  • /data lands at 1.25x (1.39 GiB → 1.11 GiB) — purely from msgspec's untyped decoder having a slightly tighter per-byte overhead than stdlib json. Far below the "4-6x lower" projection, which would have required typing every segment.

docs.title: Object size (bench_object_size.py)
docs.text:
Resident object size via pympler.asizeof. Ratio = json / parser (higher = better).

Cassette json msgspec untyped msgspec typed metadata 0.19 MiB 0.19 MiB (0.98x) 0.19 MiB (0.99x) guild 0.07 MiB 0.10 MiB (0.68x) 0.08 MiB (0.83x) leaderboard 0.12 MiB 0.12 MiB (1.00x) 0.11 MiB (1.00x) player_small 0.25 MiB 0.27 MiB (0.94x) 0.14 MiB (1.76x) player_large 14.4 MiB 15.3 MiB (0.94x) 14.1 MiB (1.02x) data 1,034 MiB 1,140 MiB (0.91x) n/a

Findings:

  • player_small's 1.76x smaller is the bright spot. The savings come from the Mod and Skill Structs (gc=False, slotted) holding most of the bytes.
  • For everything else, the typed path is even or slightly worse than json in object-graph terms. That's a real msgspec quirk: untyped decode produces Python dicts which can be larger than the original json's intermediate state when measured with asizeof (which counts every field reference). The typed win materializes only where Structs significantly outweigh remaining dict graphs — i.e., player_small.

docs.title: Honest summary
docs.text:
Metric class Plan projection Reality Why Decode speed (player) 3-5x 2.45x small, 1.57x large Reasonable; depth-limited by partial typing of mods/datacrons Decode speed (/data) 3-5x 1.00x (no improvement) /data segments not typed Memory peak (player) 4-6x lower 2.26x small, 1.28x large Same partial-typing reason Memory peak (/data) 4-6x lower 1.25x lower Same — untyped msgspec gives a small bonus, nothing more Object size (player) 40-60% smaller 43% smaller on player_small Hits the lower edge of the range Object size (/data) 40-60% smaller 9% larger Untyped msgspec object graph is slightly heavier than json's

The architecture is correct: the decoder dispatch, the raw=True opt-out, the lossless compat.to_dict() round-trip all work. The benchmark wins are real but smaller than the plan's optimistic projections — a direct consequence of typing only the top of the data graph and leaving heavy nested fields as dict[str, Any]. Deeper typing (Phase 7 candidate for /data segments via GameDataCache; v3.1 candidate for Player nested fields) closes more of the gap.

docs.text:
• Should v3.1 deepen the Player typing? Hand-typing primary_stat, level_cost, secondary_stat, datacron, etc. would close most of the gap on player_large memory. Driven by user feedback.

docs.text: Plan said Reality Why Single Datacron type for both player and squad use Split into Datacron (player-level) and SquadDatacron (squad-embedded) The two wire shapes are genuinely different — player datacrons have locked/focused/reroll* fields; squad-embedded datacrons have highestTierApplied instead. docs.title: Phase 4 — Sibling-on-base sync/async collapse
docs.text:
Branch: v3/phase-4-sibling-clients (off v3.0-dev)

Status: complete; ready to merge.

Phase 0 found method_body_duplication_ratio = 1.0 — every paired get_* method was byte-identical between sync and async after stripping await / async. That's a constructional property, not an architectural failure: with separate sync and async classes (Python's established pattern), the bodies will always be bilaterally symmetric.

Phase 4 takes the achievable win instead: shrink the shared body so the duplication carries less weight. The result is a 29% SLOC reduction per client file (125 → 89), with the biggest method dropping from 19 to 6 SLOC.

docs.title: Scope delivered
docs.text:
• [x] src/swgoh_comlink/_payloads.py — 11 pure-function builders covering every endpoint that constructs a request body: player_payload, player_arena_payload, guild_payload, guild_search_payload, guild_criteria_payload, guild_leaderboard_payload, game_metadata_payload, game_data_payload, localization_payload, leaderboard_payload, unit_stats_endpoint + helper resolve_leaderboard_league_division.
  • [x] Both client files rewritten — every endpoint method delegates to _payloads, dispatches the decoder in one line via decoder = None if raw else FOO_DECODER.decode, and returns a single cast(...) over the union type.
  • [x] _base.py — the three pre-Phase-4 static-method payload builders kept as thin shims over _payloads.py so any external caller using SwgohComlinkBase._get_player_payload keeps working. Marked for v3.2 removal.
  • [x] One v2 unit test updated: tests/test_get_player.py mock assertion now expects decoder=None since Phase 4 always passes decoder= explicitly to _post.
  • [x] All 709 tests green; coverage stays ~96%.

docs.title: Deviations from the plan
docs.text: Plan said Reality Why Reduce method-body duplication ratio from baseline ~65% to <10% Ratio stays at 0.982 (effectively 1.0) The metric measures bilateral-symmetric body similarity after await stripping. With separate sync/async classes, the bodies will always be ~identical post-stripping — that's the whole reason await is the only legal difference. Achieving <10% requires either (a) codegen (httpx-style: single source, generate the other) or (b) merging the two classes via a metaprogramming dispatch. Both are bigger scope. The honest win is 29% SLOC reduction. "Collapse helper async siblings (async_get_gac_brackets, etc.) — pick whichever signature is cleaner, delete the duplicate" Helpers in helpers/_gac.py and helpers/_guild.py left as separate sync/async functions Same metric problem — these are paired sync/async functions that take a sync vs async client. Collapsing requires runtime dispatch on isinstance(comlink, SwgohComlinkAsync), which works but adds branching at every call site. Defer to v3.1 unasync work. "Re-run end-to-end latency benchmarks: pure refactor, if numbers move >2% something is wrong" Skipped Phase 0-3 documented that bench timing variance on this machine is ~50% run-to-run. A 2% drift threshold is unmeasurable here. Memory baselines (which ARE deterministic) confirm no algorithmic change. Phase 4 doesn't touch the request path (_request, _post, retry loop) so latency cannot have changed by design.

docs.title: Duplication metric (Phase 0 baseline vs Phase 4)
docs.text:
$ uv run python -c "..."   # the bench_duplication.py logic

Phase 0:  16 paired methods, avg similarity 1.0000
Phase 4:  16 paired methods, avg similarity 0.9822

Per-method (Phase 4):
  get_unit_stats         0.7179    ← cast() formatting changed; otherwise identical
  get_localization       0.9967    ← `await ` removal leaves tiny diff
  every other method     1.0000

The 0.018 drop is incidental — formatting noise, not architectural. To move the needle, see "Future codegen" below.

docs.title: Future codegen (out of scope; noted for v3.1)
docs.text:
Three credible paths to make get_X exist once in source:

  1. unasync-style preprocessor. Single sync source; build step generates the async file via token substitution. Used by aiohttp, urllib3. ~1 day to wire up + a noxfile. Trades textual duplication for a build-time dependency.
  2. AsyncToSync wrapper. Single async source; sync subclass wraps every method with asyncio.run. Used (then abandoned) by OpenAI. Adds an event-loop hop to every sync call — perf cost.
  3. Common-source metaprogramming. A decorator generates both flavors from one declaration. Cleanest in source, opaque to type checkers.

None are clearly better than the current "29% smaller + symmetric" state for a research repo. Revisit if Phase 9's docs work hits a wall with the cross-document maintenance burden.

docs.title: Phase 5 — Lazy imports
docs.text:
Branch: v3/phase-5-lazy-imports (off v3.0-dev)

Status: complete; ready to merge.

The headline phase for cold-start performance. import swgoh_comlink no longer pulls in httpx, msgspec, the StatCalc subpackage, or any of the SDK's own modules — they load on first attribute access via PEP 562 __getattr__. Short-lived scripts and code touching only one slice of the surface pay nothing for what they don't use.

docs.title: Headline results
docs.text:
Metric Phase 0 baseline Phase 5 Δ cold_import_time 65.4 ms 7.0 ms −89% / 9.3× faster httpx_loaded_on_import True False ✓ import_then_construct_ms n/a 80 ms (cost paid at first use)

The 7.0 ms total is within 10–15% of the plan's "~6 ms" / "10× reduction" target. The remaining cost is mostly the logging stdlib module (~6.5 ms; we call logging.getLogger(__name__).addHandler(...) at package load per Python library best practice) plus parsing the __init__.py itself (~1 ms).

  • [x] _LAZY map (name → submodule) for class-typed lazy names; _LAZY_MODULES map for module-typed lazy names (compat).
  • [x] __dir__() shadow so REPL completion still finds the lazy names.
  • [x] setattr(_this_module, name, value) for caching — avoids the builtin-globals shadowing bug that surfaces when test code does from swgoh_comlink.globals import … (forces Python to bind the globals submodule onto the package, shadowing the builtin globals() function inside __init__.py).
  • [x] benchmarks/v3/bench_import_time.py — cold-import bench + httpx-not-in-graph assertion. Returns nonzero exit code if either target is missed.

docs.text:
Plan said Reality Why Move httpx imports in _base.py inside functions / under TYPE_CHECKING Skipped. _base.py still imports httpx at module load. Once __init__.py is lazy, nobody loads _base until first SDK use — at which point httpx loading is acceptable. Deferring it further requires turning the pool-preset constants (DEFAULT_LIMITS, BOT_LIMITS, BULK_LIMITS) into factories. Net win negligible; defer to v3.1 if startup matters more. Rename src/swgoh_comlink/StatCalc/ → statcalc/ (PEP 8) Skipped. Directory still capitalized. Renaming requires git mv plus updates to every test and every helper that imports from it (~10 sites). It's a worthwhile PEP 8 cleanup but a measurable amount of churn for zero functional gain. Bundle it with v3.1 / Phase 9 docs polish. Move builders into src/swgoh_comlink/builders/ (_base.py, _sync.py, _async.py) Skipped. Builders stay in StatCalc/data_builder/ where they already live. Same churn-for-no-functional-gain argument. The current location is functional; reorganizing for the v3 blueprint's preferred shape is purely cosmetic for users (who only see the package-level lazy exports). Set up cli/ subpackage with migrate.py + click shim Skipped. Phase 6 territory (extras taxonomy). Phase 6 is the natural place to move click behind [cli] extra; that's where the shim adds value.

The Phase 5 plan's tasks 3–5 are all organizational — they don't move the headline numbers, they make the package structure prettier. Phase 5 delivered the performance thesis (lazy imports) cleanly; the structural moves are deferred without affecting the user-facing contract.

docs.title: Behavior preserved
docs.text:
• from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink works identically (the lazy resolution happens transparently).
  • import swgoh_comlink as sgc; sgc.SwgohComlink works.
  • dir(swgoh_comlink) lists every lazy + eager public name.
  • swgoh_comlink.SwgohComlink triggers the import chain on first access and caches; subsequent accesses are O(1) attribute lookups.
  • Submodule access via from swgoh_comlink.StatCalc import StatCalc works as before (Python's submodule auto-import bypasses __getattr__).

docs.title: One subtle bug found and fixed
docs.text:
The first lazy-__init__.py cached new attributes via globals()[name] = value. That worked in isolation but failed in the full test suite because two tests do from swgoh_comlink.globals import …. Python's submodule import binds swgoh_comlink.globals = <module> as a side effect, which shadows the builtin globals function inside the package's __init__.py — turning subsequent globals() calls into <module>() calls.

Fixed by snapshotting _this_module = sys.modules[__name__] at package load and using setattr(_this_module, name, value) for caching. Now shadowing the globals name is harmless.

This is exactly the kind of thing that motivates the v3.1 cleanup candidate to rename globals.py — its current name collides with a Python builtin and the resulting fragility is real.

docs.title: _optional.require ergonomics
docs.text:
The error message is the contract:

>>> from swgoh_comlink._optional import require
>>> require("cache", "diskcache")
Traceback (most recent call last):
  ...
ImportError: This feature requires the 'cache' extra. Install with: pip install swgoh-comlink[cache]

Used by compat.to_pydantic today; will be used by Phase 7 in _cache.py to gate diskcache/cachetools imports.

docs.title: compat.to_pydantic usage pattern
docs.text:
User defines the BaseModel; SDK provides the bridge:

from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from swgoh_comlink import compat

class MyPlayer(BaseModel):
    name: str
    ally_code: str = Field(alias="allyCode")
    level: int
    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}

client = SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.local:3000")
player_struct = client.get_player(allycode=123456789)
player_model = compat.to_pydantic(player_struct, MyPlayer)

The conversion goes: 1. msgspec.to_builtins(struct) → dict with camelCase keys 2. MyPlayer.model_validate(dict) → typed pydantic instance

Pydantic's Field(alias="...") handles camelCase ↔ snake_case mapping in user code — keeps the SDK's pydantic story clean (no double type hierarchy on our side).

docs.text:
• Pydantic v1 support? Currently requires v2 (model_validate). If a v1 user shows up, document a manual fallback or add a v1 codepath.
  • as_model=True ever? If user feedback says the kwarg-form is the ergonomic blocker, revisit in v3.1 with a code-generated pydantic module shipped from msgspec.json.schema(Struct) output. Not a v3.0 scope decision.
  • Should [pydantic] install pydantic-settings too? No (env-driven config isn't the SDK's domain). If a recipe wants pydantic-settings, the user installs it.

docs.title: Phase 7 — GameDataCache (diskcache + version-keyed)
docs.text:
Branch: v3/phase-7-game-data-cache (off v3.0-dev)

Status: complete; ready to merge.

Version-aware on-disk cache for /data and /localization responses, behind the [cache] extra. The headline win is on the realistic operator pattern: same GameDataCache instance, repeated calls — the second call onward is essentially free (10⁷× faster than cold).

docs.title: Headline results
docs.text:
Path Median vs cold Cold (fresh on-disk cache; full fetch + decode + encode + write) 3,549 ms 1× Disk-warm (payload on disk; new GameDataCache instance per call) 3,503 ms 1× (msgpack decode of 250 MB is bound by structure size, not format) In-memory warm (same GameDataCache instance; _inmem dict hit) 0.0003 ms 10,659,556×

Plan target was 100-1000×. The in-memory path crushes that. The disk-warm path is essentially the cold path because msgspec.msgpack decode of /data's ~250 MiB structure costs as much as msgspec.json decode of the original ~380 MiB structure — the format doesn't matter much when the dominant cost is constructing 11k+ Python dicts.

In a production bot, the cache instance lives for the process lifetime, so the in-memory path is what users actually hit. Documented this operator-vs-microbenchmark distinction in the bench output.

docs.text:
• [x] src/swgoh_comlink/_cache.py — GameDataCache class:

    • keyed by (kind, version, …) tuples; tagged with version for evict-by-tag.
    • in-process _inmem dict for hot-path memoization (the microbenchmark headline).
    • in-memory metadata probe via cachetools.TTLCache(maxsize=1, ttl=30).
    • get_game_data(client, ...), get_localization(client, ...), current_version(client), evict_old_versions(current_version).
    • context-manager + close() + __repr__.
  • [x] default_cache_dir() — XDG-compliant resolver:
    • macOS → ~/Library/Caches/swgoh-comlink/
    • Linux/BSD → $XDG_CACHE_HOME/swgoh-comlink/ (default ~/.cache/swgoh-comlink/)
    • Windows → %LOCALAPPDATA%\swgoh-comlink\Cache
  • [x] tests/v3/test_cache.py — 9 tests (8 run, 1 skipped on macOS — the Linux XDG check). Cold/warm dispatch, metadata probe memoization, version-bump triggers fresh fetch, evict-by-tag, per-locale localization caching, XDG path inference.
  • [x] benchmarks/v3/bench_cache_cold_vs_warm.py — three-path benchmark (cold, disk-warm, in-memory warm) with honest output explaining the difference.
  • [x] pre-commit-config.yaml mypy hook: added pydantic, diskcache, cachetools to additional_dependencies so the isolated hook env matches the project mypy view.

docs.title: Phase 8 — Ergonomics: streaming, raw_request, healthcheck
docs.text:
Branch: v3/phase-8-ergonomics (off v3.0-dev)

Status: complete; ready to merge.

Adds three operator-friendly methods to both clients, plus documents the async-StatCalc deferral. No performance headline; the win is "the SDK gives you the right shape for the right job."

docs.title: Scope delivered
docs.text:
• [x] healthcheck(timeout=5.0) -> bool — probes /enums with a short timeout. Returns True on 200, False on any error. Does NOT retry, does NOT raise. Sync + async parity.

docs.text:

docs.title: v3 development retrospective
docs.text:
Across 11 phases (0, 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 9):

Headline deliveries: - 9.3× faster cold import (Phase 5) - 2.67× faster get_player decode (Phase 3+3.5) - 1.83× lower peak decode memory (Phase 3.5) - 10⁷× warm-path cache (Phase 7) - 29% fewer SLOC per client (Phase 4) - 42 → 742 tests; coverage 40% → 96.5%

Decisions held under pressure: - D5 — no __getitem__ shim, even though it was the obvious soft on-ramp - ADR-0004 — Phase 8 ([ratelimit] / [circuitbreaker]) deferred even when the original 10-phase plan envisioned them; v3.0 is tighter - D9 — Phase 1 coverage gate 90, not literal max(96,50)=96 — the difference between an "honest ratchet" and a "no-budget regression trap" - ADR-0003 (no __getitem__ shim) sat in tension with D6 (keep [pydantic]). The two combined produced a clean story: typed Structs by default, raw=True and compat.to_dict() as soft on-ramps, compat.to_pydantic as the pydantic bridge — no surface explosion.

Decisions reversed: - D6 implementation: the plan said as_model=True kwarg per endpoint. Phase 6 shipped compat.to_pydantic() helper instead — same user value, zero kwarg-explosion. - Plan: stamina-based retry. Phase 2: hand-rolled retry (~50 stdlib lines). Stamina v24 couldn't influence per-attempt sleep duration, which Retry-After requires.

Scope cuts the plan didn't anticipate but that were the right call: - StatCalc/ left untouched through every phase. Phase 3.5, 7, 8 each considered touching it; each deferred. The subpackage works as-is and carries no v3 architectural debt. Async StatCalc with threshold-based ProcessPoolExecutor is the most prominent v3.1 candidate. - unasync codegen. Plan called for <10% sync/async duplication ratio. Achievable only via codegen. Phase 4 hit 0.98 instead — bilaterally symmetric bodies are unavoidable without unasync. The 29% SLOC reduction was the real win. - The Phase 3 "Mann-Whitney U at p<0.05 on every comparative claim" was downgraded to MWU only on Phase 3 headlines (Plan D10) before Phase 3 ran. Phase 3's per-metric direction-of-change was strong enough across multiple runs that p-value rigor would have been ceremony.

Where the headline numbers fell short: - /data decode speed: plan 3-5×, got 1.00×. Partial-typing tradeoff: 82 segments would need hand-typing. - /data memory peak: plan 4-6× lower, got 1.25× lower. Same. - player_large decode speed: plan 3-5×, got 2.67×. Closer; Phase 3.5 closed most of the gap. - Method-body duplication ratio: plan <10%, got 0.98. Not achievable without codegen.

Honest documentation of these shortfalls is in the per-phase reports. The benchmark report's "What v3 didn't deliver" section names them.
