docs.title: Bulk analyst
docs.text: A short-lived script that pulls a lot of players, runs analysis, writes a report, exits. Different needs from a long-running bot: pool sized for concurrency, no need for a persistent cache (the data is consumed once), [pydantic] for the report's typed model.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
import asyncio
from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlinkAsync  # Struct returns

async def main():
    async with SwgohComlinkAsync(
        url="http://comlink.local:3000",
        profile="bulk",          # max_connections=500, keepalive 60s
        # min_interval spaces calls to one endpoint; retries cover rate
        # refusals and HTTP 503 (opt-in; default is a single attempt).
        retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=5, min_interval=0.1),
    ) as client:
        if not await client.healthcheck(timeout=5.0):
            return 2
        await run_analysis(client)
    return 0

docs.title: Fan-out with asyncio.Semaphore
docs.text:
async def run_analysis(client):
    allies = load_ally_codes_from_csv("input.csv")  # ~1000 entries

    # 10 in-flight at once — past this comlink starts rate-limiting
    # (the official limit is ~80/s on /player + 18/s on others, so 10
    # concurrent calls is a comfortable headroom)
    sem = asyncio.Semaphore(10)

    async def one(ally: int):  # returns a Player Struct
        async with sem:
            return await client.get_player(allycode=ally)

    players = await asyncio.gather(*(one(a) for a in allies))

    # Attribute access throughout; no dict indexing
    for p in players:
        print(p.name, p.guild_name, len(p.roster_unit))

docs.title: Optional: typed pydantic models for the report
docs.text:
# pip install swgoh-comlink[pydantic]
from pydantic import BaseModel, Field
from swgoh_comlink import compat

class PlayerSummary(BaseModel):
    name: str
    ally_code: str = Field(alias="allyCode")
    guild_name: str = Field(alias="guildName")
    roster_size: int
    model_config = {"populate_by_name": True}

def summarize(player) -> PlayerSummary:
    raw = compat.to_dict(player)  # camelCase dict
    raw["roster_size"] = len(raw["rosterUnit"])
    return PlayerSummary.model_validate(raw)

(For deeper integration, define a richer BaseModel covering all the fields you need and validate the whole player at once.)

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• Profile. "bulk" is the right preset: max_connections=500 handles a bigger fan-out before httpx queues.
  • Cache. Skip GameDataCache here — you're not making repeat /data calls. If you DO need /data once, just call client.get_game_data() directly.
  • Memory. With gc=False Struct leaves (Phase 3.5), a fully-loaded Player Struct is ~30% smaller than the v2 dict. For 1000 players in memory simultaneously the win is real (5-10 MiB).

docs.title: What's NOT here
docs.text:
• aiometer-based rate limiting. v3.1 candidate. For now, the Semaphore + gather pattern above is what you'd write anyway.
  • Resume-on-failure for partial runs. Add your own checkpoint file if a single bad input shouldn't tank the whole script.

docs.title: Short-lived CLI script
docs.text: A one-shot script invoked from a shell pipeline or argparse CLI. Cold import time matters; nothing else.

docs.title: The numbers that justify this recipe
docs.text:
• v2 import swgoh_comlink: ~65 ms (drags httpx, msgspec, StatCalc, helpers).
  • v3 import swgoh_comlink: ~7 ms (PEP 562 lazy __getattr__).

For a script that runs in 100 ms total, a 60 ms import cost was a non-trivial fraction. v3 makes the import effectively free for scripts that don't use the full SDK surface.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
#!/usr/bin/env python3
"""Print a player's roster size from the command line."""
from __future__ import annotations
import sys
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink  # typed surface: get_player returns a Player Struct

def main() -> int:
    allycode = int(sys.argv[1])
    with SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.local:3000") as client:
        # No retry= argument: the default is one attempt and no waiting, so a
        # one-shot script fails fast (don't burn 30 seconds on a transient failure)
        try:
            player = client.get_player(allycode=allycode)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"error: {e}", file=sys.stderr)
            return 1
        print(f"{player.name}: {len(player.roster_unit)} units")
    return 0

if __name__ == "__main__":
    sys.exit(main())

docs.title: What you can skip
docs.text:
• No [cache] — the cache is only valuable across calls; a single-shot script doesn't benefit.
  • No profile="bot" / "bulk" — default pool is fine for one call.
  • No healthcheck() — if comlink is down, the actual call fails fast (the default is one attempt, no retries). A separate probe just doubles your latency.

docs.title: What v3 gives you for free
docs.text:
• ~7 ms cold import (vs ~65 ms in v2). Anything else in your script dominates the wall time.
  • Typed return — player.name, len(player.roster_unit) work without type-narrowing dance.
  • Retries are opt-in (retry=RetryPolicy(...)), so this script fails fast by default. Add a policy only if you expect to hit rate refusals.

docs.title: When to add complexity back
docs.text:
• You start making /data calls (one cache call across the per-invoke lifetime gives you nothing; /data over the wire is ~3-7s). Switch to a long-running pattern.
  • Your script runs as part of a deployment with strict timeouts. Add healthcheck(timeout=1.0) if you'd rather fail before the comlink call than during it.

docs.title: Long-running bot
docs.text: A bot that lives for the process lifetime, makes many calls per minute, and needs to survive transient comlink hiccups. The v3 features that matter here are: profile="bot", an opt-in RetryPolicy, healthcheck for startup, and GameDataCache for /data//localization.

docs.title: Setup
docs.text:
from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy
from swgoh_comlink._cache import GameDataCache  # requires [cache] extra
from swgoh_comlink.exceptions import SwgohComlinkException
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink  # Struct returns

client = SwgohComlink(
    url="http://comlink.local:3000",
    profile="bot",          # keepalive 120s, larger pool
    # Opt-in (default None = one attempt): retry rate refusals and HTTP 503,
    # honour Retry-After, and space calls to one endpoint at least 0.4 s apart.
    retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=5, min_interval=0.4),
)

# Startup probe — fail fast if comlink is down
if not client.healthcheck(timeout=5.0):
    raise SystemExit("comlink unreachable; check the service")

cache = GameDataCache()  # XDG default: ~/Library/Caches/swgoh-comlink/ (macOS)

docs.title: Per-tick loop
docs.text:
while True:
    # /data + /localization come from the cache; first call per process
    # hits the wire, every later call within the same process is a
    # microsecond-scale dict lookup.
    game_data = cache.get_game_data(client)
    loc = cache.get_localization(client, locale="ENG_US")

    # /player is uncached (the data changes per call by design)
    for ally in tracked_allies:
        try:
            player = client.get_player(allycode=ally)
        except SwgohComlinkException:
            # Rate refusals / 503 were already retried per the RetryPolicy;
            # just log and skip
            log.exception("get_player failed for %s", ally)
            continue
        process(player, game_data)  # attribute access throughout

    time.sleep(60)

docs.title: Operational notes
docs.text:
• Cache instance lifetime. Keep ONE GameDataCache for the process lifetime. The in-memory memo only benefits same-instance calls.
  • Cache eviction. Call cache.evict_old_versions(cache.current_version(client)) on a schedule (e.g. daily) to clean up stale game-data versions. Diskcache won't grow unbounded — the _inmem dict resets after each evict.
  • Retry policy. Retries are opt-in. With RetryPolicy(attempts=5) a rate refusal (HTTP 429 / Rate exceeded!) or HTTP 503 is retried, waiting for Retry-After (capped at max_retry_after) or the next backoff step (5, 10, 20, 40 s) plus jitter. Any other error is raised at once as a typed SwgohComlinkHTTPError. A rate refusal also holds back that endpoint on the whole client, so concurrent tasks back off together. Adjust per call site with client.with_options(retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=8)). See Retries and pacing.
  • Connection pool. profile="bot" is tuned for low-frequency, long-lived patterns: keepalive_expiry=120s, max_connections=200, max_keepalive_connections=50. Default would also work; this preset is marginally better when you're calling every minute or two and TCP/TLS handshakes start to matter.

docs.title: Async variant (SwgohComlinkAsync + async cache)
docs.text:
Same pattern, different surface. GameDataCache exposes a* twins of every client-touching method and an async with lifecycle. The disk store and in-memory memo are shared with the sync surface, so a sync warmup script can populate the cache an async bot reads.

import asyncio
from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy
from swgoh_comlink._cache import GameDataCache
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlinkAsync

async def main():
    async with (
        SwgohComlinkAsync(
            url="http://comlink.local:3000",
            profile="bot",
            retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=5, min_interval=0.4),
        ) as client,
        GameDataCache() as cache,
    ):
        if not await client.healthcheck(timeout=5.0):
            raise SystemExit("comlink unreachable")

        while True:
            game_data = await cache.aget_game_data(client)
            loc = await cache.aget_localization(client, locale="ENG_US")

            tasks = [client.get_player(allycode=a) for a in tracked_allies]
            for player in await asyncio.gather(*tasks, return_exceptions=True):
                if isinstance(player, Exception):
                    log.exception("get_player failed: %s", player)
                    continue
                process(player, game_data)

            await asyncio.sleep(60)

asyncio.run(main())

Internals: aget_game_data / aget_localization / acurrent_version / aevict_old_versions / aclose wrap the blocking diskcache and msgpack operations in asyncio.to_thread, so the event loop stays responsive on cold and disk-warm paths. In-memory hits stay synchronous (nanosecond-scale dict access).

docs.title: What's NOT here
docs.text:
• Rate limiting. [ratelimit] is deferred to v3.1 (ADR-0004). Until then, see operator-side-concurrency.md for the asyncio.Semaphore pattern.
  • Circuit breaker. Same deferral. If you want to stop hammering comlink after N consecutive failures, the operator code wraps the loop with a simple counter today.

docs.title: Operator-side concurrency control (in lieu of [ratelimit])
docs.text: v3.0 does NOT ship [ratelimit] — that extra is deferred to v3.1 (ADR-0004). This recipe covers the patterns that get you 80% of the value with zero v3.0 dependencies.

docs.title: When you need it
docs.text:
• Calling comlink from a bot that fans out across many players (e.g. guild-wide /player pulls).
  • Comlink's documented limits: ~80 req/s on /player, ~18 req/s on most other endpoints.
  • Hitting the limit returns HTTP 429 (or the game's Rate exceeded! refusal) with Retry-After. Pass retry=RetryPolicy(...) and the client honors the header, but you'd rather not be relying on retry for normal traffic.

docs.title: Pattern 1: asyncio.Semaphore
docs.text:
import asyncio
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlinkAsync

async def fetch_many(allies: list[int]) -> list:
    async with SwgohComlinkAsync(url="http://comlink.local:3000") as client:
        # In-flight concurrency cap. 10 is a safe number under the
        # 80/s /player limit at typical latency (~50ms per call).
        sem = asyncio.Semaphore(10)

        async def one(ally: int):
            async with sem:
                return await client.get_player(allycode=ally)

        return await asyncio.gather(*(one(a) for a in allies))

docs.title: Pattern 2: token-bucket rate limiter (vendored)
docs.text:
If you want strict requests-per-second, hand-roll a small token bucket:

import asyncio
import time

class TokenBucket:
    """Crude async token bucket. Drop-in replacement until v3.1 [ratelimit]."""

    def __init__(self, rate: float, capacity: int | None = None) -> None:
        self.rate = rate                           # tokens / second
        self.capacity = capacity or max(1, int(rate))
        self._tokens = float(self.capacity)
        self._last = time.monotonic()
        self._lock = asyncio.Lock()

    async def acquire(self, tokens: int = 1) -> None:
        async with self._lock:
            now = time.monotonic()
            self._tokens = min(self.capacity, self._tokens + (now - self._last) * self.rate)
            self._last = now
            if self._tokens >= tokens:
                self._tokens -= tokens
                return
            need = tokens - self._tokens
            self._tokens = 0
        # Sleep OUTSIDE the lock so other tasks can refill.
        await asyncio.sleep(need / self.rate)

# Usage
player_bucket = TokenBucket(rate=80)   # 80/s for /player
generic_bucket = TokenBucket(rate=18)  # 18/s for everything else

async def safe_get_player(client, ally):
    await player_bucket.acquire()
    return await client.get_player(allycode=ally)

For sync code, swap asyncio.Lock → threading.Lock, asyncio.sleep → time.sleep.

docs.title: Pattern 3: circuit-breaker via failure counter
docs.text:
In lieu of [circuitbreaker]:

class FailureCounter:
    """Stop sending requests after N consecutive failures, retry after cool-down."""

    def __init__(self, threshold: int = 5, cooldown_seconds: float = 30) -> None:
        self.threshold = threshold
        self.cooldown = cooldown_seconds
        self._fails = 0
        self._opened_at: float | None = None

    def allow(self) -> bool:
        if self._opened_at is None:
            return True
        if time.monotonic() - self._opened_at > self.cooldown:
            # Half-open: let one call through to probe
            self._opened_at = None
            self._fails = 0
            return True
        return False

    def succeeded(self) -> None:
        self._fails = 0
        self._opened_at = None

    def failed(self) -> None:
        self._fails += 1
        if self._fails >= self.threshold:
            self._opened_at = time.monotonic()


breaker = FailureCounter(threshold=5, cooldown_seconds=60)

def safely_get_player(client, ally):
    if not breaker.allow():
        raise RuntimeError("circuit open; skipping comlink call")
    try:
        p = client.get_player(allycode=ally)
        breaker.succeeded()
        return p
    except SwgohComlinkException:
        breaker.failed()
        raise

docs.title: When to migrate to [ratelimit] / [circuitbreaker]
docs.text: When you have ≥2 production operators independently asking for the same features, that's the signal to land v3.1's [ratelimit] + [circuitbreaker] extras (which would wrap aiometer/aiolimiter and purgatory respectively behind the same install-hint pattern Phase 6 set up).

docs.title: Typed access to /data segments
docs.text: /data returns 80+ segments. v3 ships typed msgspec.Structs for 14 of them (the high-value ones operators actually inspect), exposed through a single generic helper. Everything else stays as dict[str, Any] — and the same helper accepts your own Struct for shapes the SDK doesn't ship.

docs.title: The helper
docs.text:
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, compat

with SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.local:3000") as client:
    raw = client.get_game_data(request_segment=0)        # unchanged: dict[str, Any]
    units = compat.decode_segment(raw, "units")           # → list[Unit]
    materials = compat.decode_segment(raw, "material")    # → list[Material]
    skills = compat.decode_segment(raw, "skill")          # → list[SkillDefinition]

The first positional argument is the dict you got back from get_game_data. The second is the top-level segment key from /data. Output is a list of typed Structs you can iterate, dot-access, and type-check.

If the segment is empty or missing, you get []. No exceptions for the common "segment absent from this request_segment" case.

docs.title: Stock segments
docs.text:
compat.STOCK_SEGMENT_TYPES lists the 14 known mappings:

Segment key Struct Approx. count units Unit 11,169 skill SkillDefinition 1,892 material Material 858 ability Ability 6,465 campaign Campaign 16 effect Effect 60,015 equipment Equipment 698 recipe Recipe 2,172 statMod StatMod 288 statModSet StatModSet 8 datacronAffixTemplateSet DatacronAffixTemplateSet 722 datacronTemplate DatacronTemplate 61 datacronSet DatacronSet 10 datacronHelpEntry DatacronHelpEntry 5

All Struct classes are importable from swgoh_comlink._models. Counts are from the recorded benchmark cassette and will drift as Capital Games adds content.

docs.title: Bring your own Struct
docs.text:
For segments the SDK doesn't ship, or when you want a smaller curated view of a stock segment, pass target= with your own Struct:

import msgspec
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink, compat

class MyTinyMaterial(msgspec.Struct, rename="camel"):
    """Just the three fields I actually care about."""
    id: str = ""
    rarity: int = 0
    tier: int = 0

with SwgohComlink(url="...") as client:
    raw = client.get_game_data(request_segment=0)
    mats = compat.decode_segment(raw, "material", target=MyTinyMaterial)
    # mats is list[MyTinyMaterial] — only the fields you defined.

Two things to know about your custom Struct:

  1. rename="camel" — the wire format is camelCase; your Python fields should be snake_case and msgspec rewrites them.
  2. Defaults on every field — forbid_unknown_fields=False is the default (Comlink ships extra fields you don't care about); make every field have a default value so partial cassettes don't break decoding.

You don't need to register your type anywhere. The helper only consults STOCK_SEGMENT_TYPES when target=None.

docs.title: Cost model
docs.text:
On the recorded /data cassette, decoded from JSON bytes:

Path Decode wall (units alone) Aggregate decode wall (all 14) dict (untyped msgspec) 950 ms ~3,290 ms typed (decode_segment) 228 ms (4.16× faster) ~1,840 ms (1.79× faster)

Aggregate memory: 0.66× the dict baseline (~34% less). Aggregate resident size: 0.66×. Per-segment numbers in docs/v3/benchmark-report.md.

The dict-input path of the helper (the common case after a GameDataCache hit) uses msgspec.convert and skips the JSON re-encode hop, so real-world cost is lower than the bench numbers.

docs.title: What's intentionally not typed
docs.text:
• The other ~70+ /data segments (battleEnvironments, xpTable, statProgression, category, helpEntry, challenge, eventSampling, warDefinition, targetingSet, requirement, powerUpBundle, raidConfig, guildRaid, guildExchangeItem, table, unlockAnnouncementDefinition, battleTargetingRule, territoryBattleDefinition, territoryWarDefinition, environmentCollection, challengeStyle, …). Use target= if you need them typed.
  • Always-empty / always-null fields within the stock segments (basicAttack, leaderAbility, limitBreak, uniqueAbility, effectIconPriorityOverride, material.raidImmediateLookup, equipment.actionLinkLookup, …). They're dropped from the typed view; forbid_unknown_fields=False keeps the SDK resilient if Capital Games re-populates them.
  • Sparse / variable-shape sub-fields (ability.aiParams, effect.persistentVfxReference, recipe.craftRequirement, …). Typed as dict[str, Any] | None rather than guessed-at Structs — drop the dict back into the typed Struct if you need attribute access.

docs.title: Recipe-vs-segment quick reference
docs.text:
• You want one fully-typed list of stock entities → decode_segment(raw, "segment_key").
  • You want only a few fields per entry, your own naming → decode_segment(raw, "segment_key", target=YourStruct).
  • You want the raw /data dict you've always had → client.get_game_data() (unchanged).
  • You want typed /data cached across runs → wrap GameDataCache around your client; decode_segment(cache.get_game_data(client), ...) works the same on the cached dict.

docs.title: Using StatCalc with the typed client
docs.text:
StatCalc ships in v3.2 with two new conveniences:

  1. Bimorphic input — calc_player_stats and calc_roster_stats accept either Comlink-format dicts (the legacy surface) OR msgspec.Struct objects from the typed client.
  2. Cached normalized game data — get_statcalc_game_data persists the normalized form across process restarts, cutting cold-start StatCalc setup from ~26 ms to ~4 ms.

Both shipped as the two "winners" from the v3.2 StatCalc research (see ADR-0006 for the six candidates that didn't ship and why).

docs.title: TL;DR — typed-client startup, hot loop, both
docs.text:
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink._cache import GameDataCache
from swgoh_comlink.StatCalc import StatCalc, get_statcalc_game_data

client = SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.local:3200")
cache = GameDataCache()                              # XDG-default dir
gd = get_statcalc_game_data(client, cache=cache)     # ~4 ms warm
sc = StatCalc(game_data=gd)

# Hot path option 1: typed Struct — convenient, +22 % per-roster cost
player = client.get_player(allycode=123456789)        # Player Struct
stats = sc.calc_player_stats(player)                  # bimorphic; returns dict

# Hot path option 2: raw dict — zero overhead, dict-typed at the seam
player_raw = client.get_player(allycode=123456789, raw=True)
stats = sc.calc_player_stats(player_raw)

docs.title: When to use which input shape
docs.text:
Caller style Recommendation Why Typed Struct, calling infrequently or for a few players per tick Hand StatCalc the Struct. v3.3 dropped the bimorphic overhead from +22.9 % to +10.1 %; for an occasional caller this is well within tolerance. Typed Struct, calling per-unit in a tight loop with thousands of units/sec client.get_player(..., raw=True). +10 % still compounds at scale. The dict surface remains the zero-overhead path. v2-style dict caller (existing code) Keep doing what you're doing. The bimorphic dispatcher's isinstance(players, msgspec.Struct) check is one branch on the dict path — zero cost.

The v3.3 typed-fastpath in src/swgoh_comlink/StatCalc/_typed_fastpath.py reads msgspec.Struct.__slots__ directly instead of walking the whole Player via msgspec.to_builtins. Only the fields StatCalc actually reads (definition_id, current_level, current_rarity, current_tier, equipment, equipped_stat_mod, relic, skill[].id, skill[].tier, and the per-Mod definition_id / primary_stat.stat / secondary_stat[].stat / tier / level) are touched — saving the per-Mod walk of fields StatCalc never reads (bonus_quantity, converted_item, sell_value, xp, …). See ADR-0007 for the full measurement and the deferred native-acceleration variants.

docs.title: What "bimorphic" buys you
docs.text:
# Pre-v3.2 — typed caller had to convert themselves
import msgspec
player_struct = client.get_player(allycode=...)        # Player Struct
player_dict = msgspec.to_builtins(player_struct)       # +~5 ms
stats = sc.calc_player_stats(player_dict)              # +~22 ms

# v3.2 — same total cost, one fewer line, no caller-side imports
player_struct = client.get_player(allycode=...)
stats = sc.calc_player_stats(player_struct)            # bimorphic

You can also hand StatCalc a list of typed Player Structs:

players = [client.get_player(allycode=a) for a in tracked_allies]
all_stats = sc.calc_player_stats(players)              # list of Structs OK

Or a list of RosterUnit Structs directly to calc_roster_stats:

player = client.get_player(allycode=...)
roster_stats = sc.calc_roster_stats(list(player.roster_unit))

docs.title: What get_statcalc_game_data buys you
docs.text:
GameDataBuilder._build_game_data(raw) does the same ~25 ms of work on every process startup, transforming raw /data into the 6 normalized tables StatCalc needs. get_statcalc_game_data plumbs that into the Phase 7 GameDataCache (msgpack on disk + in-process memo), keyed by the upstream game version. After the first call, every process startup just msgpack-decodes the cached normalized form (~4 ms).

from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink
from swgoh_comlink._cache import GameDataCache
from swgoh_comlink.StatCalc import StatCalc, get_statcalc_game_data

client = SwgohComlink(url="http://comlink.local:3200")
cache = GameDataCache()

# First process startup after a game-version bump:
#   - fetches raw /data (cached by GameDataCache from then on)
#   - runs GameDataBuilder._build_game_data    ~25 ms
#   - persists the normalized form (~120 KB on disk)
# Every subsequent process startup:
#   - msgpack-decodes the normalized form     ~4 ms

gd = get_statcalc_game_data(client, cache=cache)
sc = StatCalc(game_data=gd)

This is a cold-start win. The hot path (calc_player_stats per-unit work) is unaffected. The optimization is most valuable for:

  • Cron jobs / scheduled tasks spawning a fresh interpreter per run.
  • AWS Lambda / Cloud Run scaling new instances on traffic.
  • CLI tools where startup latency is user-visible.

Long-running bots that init StatCalc once and reuse it for hours won't see a meaningful difference here — for those, focus on the hot-path / bimorphic choice above.

docs.title: What we evaluated and didn't ship
docs.text:
Six other candidates were considered, prototyped or mechanism-checked, and rejected on measured evidence:

  • Partial-conversion adapter and accessor-subclass alternatives for bimorphic input — within ±1 % of the shipped boundary check.
  • ProcessPoolExecutor fan-out for calc_roster_stats — IPC break-even exceeds per-unit work; regresses on player_large.
  • Typed-Struct game_data tables — micro-bench established ~1.3 % hot-path ceiling vs the 10 % bar.
  • Direct consumption of v3.1 typed /data segments — higher refactor cost than the Struct-tables variant, with the plan's own estimated payoff range including regression.
  • Hot-table index restructuring — 5.7 % vs 10 % bar; aggressive variant breaks parity on mod-set bonuses.

Full audit, measurements, and decision rationale in ADR-0006.

docs.title: See also
docs.text:
• docs/v3/recipes/long-running-bot.md — pairs GameDataCache with an opt-in RetryPolicy and a startup healthcheck.
  • docs/v3/migration.md — v2 → v3 upgrade path.
  • docs/v3/codegen.md — the typed/dict client split.

docs.title: Runbook — publishing the v3.0.0a1 alpha (fork-hosted)
docs.text:
Operator checklist for cutting the first public v3 alpha per ADR-0008 (including the 2026-07-12 fork-hosting addendum). Everything below is executed by the maintainer; nothing here runs automatically.

Preconditions (already true as of this writing):

  • All release prep is committed on the local release/v3.0.0a1 branch.
  • docs/v3/releases/v3.0.0a1.md exists — alpha-release.yml uses it as the GitHub Release body (body_path), so the run fails without it.
  • Local gates are green: ruff, ty, codegen drift, pytest (≥ 95 % coverage gate), uv build.

docs.title: 1. Create the fork
docs.text:
gh repo fork swgoh-utils/comlink-python --clone=false

Creates MarTrepodi/comlink-python (public — forks of public repos cannot be private; pushing the branch publishes the full v3 history).

docs.title: 2. Push the release branch to the fork
docs.text:
cd ~/code/comlink-python-v3
git remote add fork https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python.git
git push fork release/v3.0.0a1

Do not push to origin (the upstream swgoh-utils repo) — that is exactly what the fork-hosting addendum avoids.

docs.title: 3. Prepare the fork's settings (one-time, in the GitHub UI)
docs.text:
1. Enable Actions — Actions are disabled by default on new forks: fork → Actions tab → enable workflows.
  2. Workflow permissions — alpha-release.yml declares contents: write (tag + Release) and id-token: write (Sigstore keyless signing) in its own permissions: block; confirm the repo setting Settings → Actions → General → Workflow permissions does not restrict below that (default "Read repository contents" is fine — job-level permissions: override it — but if the org policy disallows elevation, switch to "Read and write permissions").
  3. Labels (optional but recommended) — dispatch the label-sync workflow so the v3 label exists before bug reports arrive.

docs.title: 4. Dry run
docs.text:
Fork → Actions → alpha-release → Run workflow:

  • Branch: release/v3.0.0a1 (the workflow guards on release/v*)
  • version: 3.0.0a1
  • dry_run: true

The run executes the full gate suite (tests, ruff, ty, codegen drift), builds wheel + sdist via hatch-vcs (SETUPTOOLS_SCM_PRETEND_VERSION), and Sigstore-signs the artifacts — but creates no tag and no Release. Inspect the run summary and the uploaded artifacts; confirm the wheel is swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a1-py3-none-any.whl and its metadata URLs point at the fork.

docs.title: 5. Real run
docs.text:
Re-dispatch with the same inputs but dry_run: false. This:

  1. Re-runs all gates and the build/sign steps
  2. Creates and pushes the annotated tag v3.0.0a1
  3. Creates the prerelease GitHub Release with the signed wheel, sdist, signature bundles, and SHA256SUMS, using docs/v3/releases/v3.0.0a1.md as the body

docs.title: 6. Post-release smoke test
docs.text:
From a clean directory (not the repo):

uv venv smoke-v3 && source smoke-v3/bin/activate
uv pip install https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a1/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a1-py3-none-any.whl
python -c "import swgoh_comlink; print(swgoh_comlink.version)"   # -> 3.0.0a1

Then one live typed call against a local comlink (e.g. run examples/typed/Sync/get_player.py with COMLINK_URL set). Also verify the git+ install path resolves the new tag:

uv pip install --dry-run "git+https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python.git@v3.0.0a1"

docs.title: 7. Announce + wrap up
docs.text:
• Confirm the Release page renders the notes and the install commands copy-paste cleanly (they should match install-alpha.md).
  • Per ADR-0008's release-branch convention, merge release/v3.0.0a1 back to its source branch with a chore(release): resume dev cycle at 3.0.0a2.dev0 commit when development resumes.

docs.title: Rollback (if the real run shipped something broken)
docs.text: A GitHub Release can be deleted and its tag removed (git push fork :refs/tags/v3.0.0a1) — but anyone may already have installed the wheel, so prefer shipping a fixed 3.0.0a2 over mutating 3.0.0a1. Deleting a Release is acceptable only in the first minutes after publication (e.g. a broken artifact discovered by the smoke test).

docs.title: swgoh-comlink v3.0.0a1 (first alpha)
docs.text:
Date: 2026-05-19 Channel: GitHub Releases only — not on PyPI. Governance: ADR-0008

The first community-tryable v3 alpha. Bundles the work from four research phases (v3.0 → v3.3) into one installable wheel. Bug reports welcome via the v3 issue label.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
This alpha is hosted on the maintainer fork MarTrepodi/comlink-python; the upstream swgoh-utils repo stays on v2.x until reintegration.

pip install https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a1/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a1-py3-none-any.whl

Or from a git ref:

pip install git+https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python.git@v3.0.0a1

Recommended: install into a dedicated virtual environment with a rollback path to the public v2.x release — see docs/v3/install-alpha.md.

The PyPI package swgoh_comlink is still v2.x — pip install --pre swgoh_comlink will NOT pick up this alpha. v3 lives only on GitHub Releases until reintegration with upstream.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text:
Phase v3.0 — Core resilience + msgspec foundation. Hand-rolled retry policy via stamina>=24.3, profiles (profile="bot", profile="cli", …). msgspec.Struct decoders for every endpoint; raw=True opt-out per call. Lazy-import __init__.py (PEP 562) so import swgoh_comlink no longer pulls httpx/msgspec eagerly — import time drops from ~110 ms to ~15 ms cold. GameDataCache (diskcache + msgpack + in-process memo) hits ~99 % cache hit rate on long-running callers.

Phase v3.1 — Typed game-data segments + async cache + client split. Generic compat.decode_segment(raw, segment) with the STOCK_SEGMENT_TYPES registry types all 14 /data segments (Units, SkillDefinition, Equipment, StatMod, StatModSet, …) as msgspec.Struct. Aggregate decode time 1.79× faster at 0.66× memory vs json.loads + dict access. aget_game_data / aget_localization on GameDataCache for async callers (40k× warm-path speedup vs cold). 2×2 client matrix (sync/async × dict/typed) code-generated from src/swgoh_comlink/_codegen/endpoints.py — see ADR-0005.

Phase v3.2 — Bimorphic StatCalc + cached game_data. StatCalc.calc_player_stats accepts either dict or msgspec.Struct; conversion happens once at the boundary. get_statcalc_game_data(client, cache=cache) caches the StatCalc-normalized game_data alongside the raw /data payload — cold-start drops from 25.7 ms to 3.6 ms (+85.9 %). See ADR-0006 for the full 8-candidate evaluation.

Phase v3.3 — Pure-Python restructure + typed-fastpath. Table- driven _calculate_mod_stats (165-line cascade → 5-line dispatch via _mod_stat_rules); lightweight _table_get; eliminated 10 per-call lambdas in _format_stats. Combined with the typed- fastpath that reads msgspec.Struct.__slots__ directly (skipping msgspec.to_builtins), the hot path is +16.3 % faster on player_large and bimorphic Struct overhead drops from +22.9 % → +10.1 %. Cython / mypyc / Rust prototypes researched but not shipped (per ADR-0007 — distribution complexity outweighed the +6-9 pp additional speed).

docs.title: Breaking changes vs v2
docs.text:
The v2 → v3 migration is documented at docs/v3/migration.md. Headlines:

  • Typed-by-default surface lives at a new import path: 
    # v2 (still works — dict-typed, byte-compatible)
from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink

# v3 typed (new — msgspec.Struct returns)
from swgoh_comlink.typed import SwgohComlink
  • click moved behind [migrate] optional extra. Only matters if you import from swgoh_comlink.migrate.
  • Python ≥ 3.11 required (was 3.10).

If your code uses from swgoh_comlink import SwgohComlink and expects dict returns, nothing changes. The dict-default client is preserved byte-for-byte from v2.

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text:
• Pure-Python only. Cython, mypyc, and Rust/PyO3 kernel prototypes exist on throwaway research branches but do NOT ship in this alpha — the 15-wheel-per-release distribution cost was judged not worth the +6-9 pp speedup. See ADR-0007 for the analysis.
  • StatCalc parallelism deferred. ProcessPoolExecutor fan-out was prototyped in v3.2 (Candidate D) but regressed on large rosters (IPC break-even exceeds per-unit work). Wait for either Cython inner loops or sub-interpreters / free-threaded Python before re-attempting. See ADR-0006.
  • Async StatCalc not implemented beyond a thin sync-inherited shell. StatCalcAsync.create() is an async factory for game-data fetch only; per-unit calc methods remain sync.
  • Bimorphic Struct overhead is +10.1 %, not ≤ 5 %. The typed-fastpath got it to +10.1 %; getting below 5 % requires a larger refactor (Struct-aware internal dispatch). For per-tick hot loops, client.get_player(..., raw=True) is still the zero-overhead path.

docs.title: Reproducing the benchmarks
docs.text:
Cassettes live in parity/ and benchmarks/v3/fixtures/. The benchmark harness is at benchmarks/v3/bench_statcalc.py:

uv sync --all-extras --dev
uv run python -m benchmarks.v3.bench_statcalc

Writes benchmarks/v3/results/phase-v3_3-baseline.json. Compare against phase-v3_3-integration.json (the shipped result) and the per-phase reports under docs/v3/phase-*-report.md.

docs.title: Reporting bugs
docs.text:
Open issues at https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/issues. The bug-report template will auto-apply the v3 label when you select v3 in the Version dropdown. Please include:

  • Python version + OS
  • swgoh_comlink.version (should print 3.0.0a1)
  • The comlink URL profile (comlink.local, localhost:3200, etc.)
  • comlink version if you know it
  • A minimal repro — for StatCalc bugs, the cassette JSON if you can share it

docs.title: Governance
docs.text:
This alpha ships under ADR-0008. The ADR explicitly forbids PyPI publication and final (non-pre-release) tags from this repo until reintegration with upstream is decided. The sunset clause requires re-evaluation by 2027-05-19 if reintegration has not completed.

For the historical context on why this is a standalone research repo at all, see ADR-0001.

docs.title: swgoh-comlink v3.0.0a2 (second alpha)
docs.text:
DRAFT. Not yet tagged or released. Verify every item against the final merge before publishing; alpha-release.yml uses this file as the GitHub Release body.

Date: TBD Channel: GitHub Releases only — not on PyPI. Governance: ADR-0008

The second community-tryable v3 alpha. 3.0.0a2 is 3.0.0a1 plus everything that shipped on the upstream v2 line as v2.3.0, v2.3.1, v2.4.0 and v2.5.0, ported onto the v3 generated clients, plus a change to the retry API (see Breaking changes since a1). Bug reports welcome via the v3 issue label.

docs.title: Install
docs.text:
This alpha is hosted on the maintainer fork MarTrepodi/comlink-python; the upstream swgoh-utils repo stays on v2.x until reintegration.

pip install https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/releases/download/v3.0.0a2/swgoh_comlink-3.0.0a2-py3-none-any.whl

Or from a git ref:

pip install git+https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python.git@v3.0.0a2

Recommended: install into a dedicated virtual environment with a rollback path to the public v2.x release — see docs/v3/install-alpha.md.

The PyPI package swgoh_comlink is still v2.x — pip install --pre swgoh_comlink will NOT pick up this alpha.

docs.title: Breaking changes since a1
docs.text:
• Retry API replaced. The max_retries= keyword (retrying 408/425/429/5xx three times by default) and its private _retry.py module are removed. Retrying is now opt-in through the keyword-only retry: RetryPolicy | None = None argument, the same policy the v2.4.0 line ships:
from swgoh_comlink import RetryPolicy, SwgohComlink

client = SwgohComlink(retry=RetryPolicy(attempts=3, min_interval=0.4))

The default (retry=None) makes exactly one attempt and never waits. A policy retries rate refusals (HTTP 429 or the game's Rate exceeded!) and HTTP 503, honours Retry-After, adds jitter, and can pace calls per endpoint. with_options(retry=...) replaces with_options(max_retries=...). The profile= connection-pool presets (default / bot / bulk) and http_client= injection are unchanged. - Typed HTTP errors. An HTTP error status now raises SwgohComlinkHTTPError or one of its subclasses (SwgohComlinkRateLimitError, SwgohComlinkUnavailableError, SwgohComlinkClientError) instead of a plain SwgohComlinkException("HTTP nnn"). str(exc) is unchanged, and all of them still subclass SwgohComlinkException. Each carries status, code, detail, retry_after and response. - get_game_data(items=...) accepts any in-range bitmask, including single collections (DataItems.UNITS); combine members with |, not +.

docs.title: Highlights
docs.text: Everything below arrived from the upstream v2.3.0 – v2.5.0 releases unless noted.

docs.title: Client
docs.text:
• Version cache. /metadata game and localization versions are cached per client (version_cache_ttl, default 3600 s; invalidate_version_cache(); get_latest_game_data_version(refresh=True)).
  • get_enums() cache. The response is cached per game data version; pass refresh=True to re-fetch.
  • RetryPolicy with attempts, backoff, jitter, max_retry_after, min_interval and unpaced_endpoints; endpoint holds after a rate refusal are shared by concurrent async callers, and a cancelled wait gives its pacing slot back.
  • Exceptions no longer log tracebacks from their constructors; typed HTTP errors are picklable and copyable.
  • py.typed marker: the package ships inline type hints (PEP 561).

docs.title: Bug fixes carried from v2.3.x – v2.5.0
docs.text:
• HMAC: the signature covers the bytes actually sent, so empty-payload signed POSTs such as get_game_metadata() validate instead of returning 403.
  • /metadata: the request sends the clientSpecs key that comlink expects (was client_specs).
  • StatCalc:
  • a mod without a set keeps its stats;
  • purchasedAbilityId is carried through raw unit normalization, so ultimate ability Galactic Power is no longer lost. This includes the typed fast path, which previously dropped it;
  • gear slots resolve for slot-less equipment entries;
  • ships with an incomplete crew are skipped instead of aborting a roster;
  • the game data builder reads bools and non-finite numbers as 0.
  • Helpers: relic offset of 2 in convert_relic_tier; UTC, timezone-aware get_arena_payout; get_playable_units tolerates missing fields and enum rarity; get_guild_members requests guild activity info; unit name keys with variant suffixes such as _NAME_V2; conquest feats whose id has no kind token; terminal and Discord styles are closed correctly; payload ints reject non-finite numbers.
  • swgoh-migrate: scan excludes are additive, glob-aware and root-relative.

docs.title: New helpers
docs.text: Territory Battle definitions, unit upgrade costs, unit abilities and named effects, item, reward and id-catalog naming (ItemNames, ItemType / CurrencyType tables), get_game_config / get_game_config_int, get_event_schedule, get_guild_activity, get_conquest_feats, calc_stamina_full_time, wire-value readers for loosely typed payload values, and sync-named helpers that accept async clients. See the helpers API reference.

docs.title: Packaging, CI and docs
docs.text:
• Python ≥ 3.11 (unchanged from a1); CI runs 3.11 – 3.14 with the optional extras installed and a 95 % coverage gate, plus the codegen drift gate.
  • ruff and ty run from uv.lock; commitlint is pinned and shares one .commitlintrc.json between pre-commit and CI; examples are linted and formatted.
  • Community files: CODE_OF_CONDUCT.md, SECURITY.md, SUPPORT.md, CITATION.cff, refreshed issue and PR templates.
  • New docs pages for the typed errors and retry policy, expanded helper reference, and a docs site workflow.

docs.title: Fixes to the a1 notes
docs.text: The 3.0.0a1 notes described the retry policy as stamina-based and said click moved behind a [migrate] extra. Neither was accurate: the a1 retry policy was hand-rolled, and no [migrate] extra existed. (The a1 retry policy is gone in this release in any case.)

docs.title: Known limitations
docs.text: The a1 limitations still apply: pure-Python only (ADR-0007), no StatCalc parallelism (ADR-0006), StatCalcAsync only makes game-data fetching async, and bimorphic Struct overhead of about 10 %.

docs.title: Reporting bugs
docs.text:
Open issues at https://github.com/MarTrepodi/comlink-python/issues with the v3 label. Please include:

  • Python version + OS
  • swgoh_comlink.version (should print 3.0.0a2)
  • The comlink URL and comlink version if you know it
  • A minimal repro — for StatCalc bugs, the cassette JSON if you can share it

docs.title: Governance
docs.text: This alpha ships under ADR-0008; PyPI publication and final (non-pre-release) tags are not permitted from this line until reintegration with upstream is decided.
